item.title: Angel Reese was mocked, doubted and hated. Now she’s dominating the Finals
item.description: Kim Mulkey kept her arm around Angel Reese ’s waist with a tight grip on her side. As the LSU women’s basketball looked up at her former star player, her face crinkled between a wide smile and the kind of pout that comes when you’re trying not to cry. “Let’s go! Two more! Two more!” Reese yelled as Mulkey beamed. Moments before that heartfelt hug, Reese had put the Atlanta Dream up 2-1 in the WNBA Finals with a 97-71 win over the Golden State Valkyries on Wednesday, Oct. 21, at State Farm Arena. The franchise is two wins away from their first championship. Reese had 21 points, 12 rebounds and three steals to lead the Dream for her third straight double-double in the Finals. She’s the youngest player to accomplish such a feat. Reese manifested this reality . Mulkey had already seen Reese do something similar for LSU in 2024, when she led the program to an NCAA title and was named as the tournament’s Most Outstanding Player. Reese’s success doesn’t come as a surprise to either of them, but likely does for the suddenly quiet crowd of Reese detractors who criticized and mocked her before and after she was taken with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2024 draft. It’s hard to think of another athlete who has silenced their doubters as effectively as Reese. Michael Jordan, Tom Brady, Lionel Messi, LeBron James and Serena Williams all weaponized criticism to do what some said they couldn’t. All-time greats, who faced moments in their careers where critics declared them too small, too old, or incapable of winning on the biggest stage. The criticism was holistic for Reeese, who has seemed to catch flack for every facet of her existence over the last few years. Now, the only outside noise Reese is being asked about is what it means to be an Atlanta sports legend. “I’ve only been here six months, so I don’t know how y’all can give me that yet,” Reese said in her postgame news conference. “My goal was to come to Atlanta and win a championship. And I think you become one of the greats and you come one of the best when you can win and impact winning. And that's all I wanted to do coming here. "Everything else really doesn't matter to me.” Reese might not care about her haters, but she’s certainly proving them wrong. Haters on her play Critics watching social media lowlights instead of actual games often attempted to boil Reese’s game down to rebounding her own missed shots – a means to detract from her historic prowess on the boards. Her rebounding accolades in the WNBA’s record books include the single-game record, single-season record and highest career rebounding average. Reese embraced the joke about her “Mebounds,” trademarked the term, launched a six-figure merchandise line, and released a pink "Mebounds" colorway for her debut Reebok Angel Reese 1 signature sneaker. But some of that rhetoric about her game still trickled down to one of Reese’s personal inspirations. In July 2025, WNBA legend Candace Parker sorted 10 WNBA players into tiers for a social media
item.content:encoded: Kim Mulkey kept her arm around Angel Reese ’s waist with a tight grip on her side. As the LSU women’s basketball looked up at her former star player, her face crinkled between a wide smile and the kind of pout that comes when you’re trying not to cry. “Let’s go! Two more! Two more!” Reese yelled as Mulkey beamed. Moments before that heartfelt hug, Reese had put the Atlanta Dream up 2-1 in the WNBA Finals with a 97-71 win over the Golden State Valkyries on Wednesday, Oct. 21, at State Farm Arena. The franchise is two wins away from their first championship. Reese had 21 points, 12 rebounds and three steals to lead the Dream for her third straight double-double in the Finals. She’s the youngest player to accomplish such a feat. Reese manifested this reality . Mulkey had already seen Reese do something similar for LSU in 2024, when she led the program to an NCAA title and was named as the tournament’s Most Outstanding Player. Reese’s success doesn’t come as a surprise to either of them, but likely does for the suddenly quiet crowd of Reese detractors who criticized and mocked her before and after she was taken with the No. 7 overall pick in the 2024 draft. It’s hard to think of another athlete who has silenced their doubters as effectively as Reese. Michael Jordan, Tom Brady, Lionel Messi, LeBron James and Serena Williams all weaponized criticism to do what some said they couldn’t. All-time greats, who faced moments in their careers where critics declared them too small, too old, or incapable of winning on the biggest stage. The criticism was holistic for Reeese, who has seemed to catch flack for every facet of her existence over the last few years. Now, the only outside noise Reese is being asked about is what it means to be an Atlanta sports legend. “I’ve only been here six months, so I don’t know how y’all can give me that yet,” Reese said in her postgame news conference. “My goal was to come to Atlanta and win a championship. And I think you become one of the greats and you come one of the best when you can win and impact winning. And that's all I wanted to do coming here. "Everything else really doesn't matter to me.” Reese might not care about her haters, but she’s certainly proving them wrong. Haters on her play Critics watching social media lowlights instead of actual games often attempted to boil Reese’s game down to rebounding her own missed shots – a means to detract from her historic prowess on the boards. Her rebounding accolades in the WNBA’s record books include the single-game record, single-season record and highest career rebounding average. Reese embraced the joke about her “Mebounds,” trademarked the term, launched a six-figure merchandise line, and released a pink "Mebounds" colorway for her debut Reebok Angel Reese 1 signature sneaker. But some of that rhetoric about her game still trickled down to one of Reese’s personal inspirations. In July 2025, WNBA legend Candace Parker sorted 10 WNBA players into tiers for a social media segment. Reese was in her second season with the Chicago Sky at the time. Parker put A'ja Wilson, Napheesa Collier and Breanna Stewart in the top tier. Caitlin Clark, Kelsey Plum, and Sabrina Ionescu went in the A tier. Arike Ogunbowale and Paige Bueckers made the B tier, and Parker put Reese in the C tier with Cameron Brink. "I put her right at that C level," Parker said in the segment. "I think Angel Reese is fantastic at her role, which is offensive rebounding." Parker later defended the decision, asking which of the nine other players on the list anyone would take Reese over. After Reese won Defensive Player of the Year, Parker revisited her take . "I was wrong," Parker said. "They're in the Final. She's Defensive Player of the Year. There's no hate. I am just giving my opinion. So congratulations to Angel Reese and the Dream for making the Finals.” Parker doesn’t believe she’s the only one who would double back if they could. “Angel Reese has been dominant … The tremendous growth that she's made and the impact," Parker said. "I'm sure there are a lot of teams in the WNBA draft that wish they could redraft." Reese averaged 14.1 points, 12.9 rebounds, and 2.7 assists during her two seasons with the Sky and was traded to the Dream in April. Her success with the Dream hasn’t come by happenstance. Reese's shot has improved because of the humility she's shown in trusting Dream coach Karl Smesko. The coach made her shoot 3-pointers in front of her teammates during practices, making three in a row, so that she would feel comfortable taking them in games. Reese made two 3-pointers in Wednesday’s Game 3. The Dreams is undefeated at 15-0 this season when she makes at least one in a game. Haters on her attitude, impact Outside of her skills, Reese has been subjected to criticisms about her attitude and assertion that she’s helped grow the game. Those criticisms are also aging poorly. In 2024, Reese was met with pushback after she spoke to reporters about her impact since she and LSU won the title over Iowa and Caitlin Clark. Her taunting and celebrations in the aftermath of that win led to relentless online abuse, including prominent social media personality Barstool Sports owner Dave Portnoy calling Reese a “classless piece of (expletive).” "People are talking about women's basketball that you'd never would think would be talking about women's basketball. People are pulling up to games. We've got celebrities coming to games [and] sold-out arenas just because of one single game," Reese said. "And just looking at that, I'll take that role. I'll take the bad guy role, and I'll continue to take that on and be that for my teammates, and I know I'll go down in history. I'll look back in 20 years and be like: 'Yeah, the reason why we're watching women's basketball is not just because of one person, it's because of me too, and I want you to realize that.' Like, it's just not ‘cause of one person. A lot of us have done so much for this game." The numbers support Reese’s reminder that she’s a viewership draw, as the Valkyries Game 1 Finals win over the Dream became the most-watched WNBA Finals Game 1 ever, averaging 2.1 million viewers and peaking at 3 million. And that “bad guy” persona Reese embraced is powering her team as well. From talking trash to Valkyries reserve center Aminata Gueye to yelling expletives in transition as she calls for the ball, Reese’s teammates have emphasized that they feed off her energy. And looking at the Valkyries’ dejected bench throughout the blowout that was Game 3, it’s felt by both teams on the league’s biggest stage. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Angel Reese was mocked, doubted and hated. Now she’s dominating the Finals

item.title: Can Jeremiah Smith still win the Heisman without Julian Sayin?
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - OCTOBER 17: Jeremiah Smith #4 of the Ohio State Buckeyes catches a pass for a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Indiana Hoosiers at Memorial Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jeremiah Smith summed up his own Heisman case in one sentence on Saturday, and he didn’t even mean to. Asked about his 38-yard touchdown on fourth and one at Indiana, the catch that turned out to be the game-winner, Smith smirked and said, “I actually ran the wrong route.” Sayin was looking for something shorter, the pocket was collapsing, and he just threw it up. Smith went up over two Indiana defenders and came down with it anyway. The route was wrong and the throw wasn’t great. Smith was simply better than everyone else. That’s the whole argument for why he can still win the Heisman, even with a true freshman throwing him the ball. The case is already built Smith is still the clear favorite. His odds have drifted since Sayin got hurt, from -220 before Indiana to somewhere between -110 and -145 depending on the sportsbook. But nobody is particularly close. Miami quarterback Darian Mensah is second at around +400, and Ole Miss quarterback Trinidad Chambliss is third on Fanduel. The resume is already there. Smith leads the country with 52 catches, ranks second with 984 receiving yards and is second with 12 touchdowns. He’s caught a touchdown in six of seven games, including four straight. He had back-to-back 200 yard games earlier this season and already owns every major receiving record at Ohio State. The Big Ten record book is next. His touchdown at Indiana was the 39th of his career, tying Braylon Edwards’ conference record. One more now breaks it. He’s also 246 yards from tying John Standeford’s Big Ten career receiving yards record of 3,788, and 247 from breaking it. Even his “quiet” game against Indiana helps his case. He finished with four catches for 68 yards, a season low, against a defense that clearly built their entire gameplan around him. He said afterward that he had extra defenders on him every play, and he still made the biggest play of the game. What changes with a freshman quarterback There’s no point pretending this doesn’t change anything. Sayin and Smith had been playing together for two years, and that kind of timing doesn’t transfer overnight. Smith said after the game that it’s going to “take time” to build the same rapport with Luke Fahey. The bigger concern isn’t Smith’s talent, it’s volume. With a freshman under center and Ja’Kobi Jackson also out after surgery, Ohio State could lean a ton on Bo Jackson and the run game. Defenses could also bracket Smith even more aggressively, daring Fahey to beat them somewhere else. That could mean fewer 200 yard afternoons and more games like Indiana. (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jeremiah Smith summed up his own Heisman case in one sentence on Saturday, and he didn’t even mean to. Asked about his 38-yard touchdown on fourth and one at Indiana, the catch that turned out to be the game-winner, Smith smirked and said, “I actually ran the wrong route.” Sayin was looking for something shorter, the pocket was collapsing, and he just threw it up. Smith went up over two Indiana defenders and came down with it anyway. The route was wrong and the throw wasn’t great. Smith was simply better than everyone else. His odds have drifted since Sayin got hurt, from -220 before Indiana to somewhere between -110 and -145 depending on the sportsbook. But nobody is particularly close. His touchdown at Indiana was the 39th of his career, tying Braylon Edwards’ conference record. One more now breaks it. He’s also 246 yards from tying John Standeford’s Big Ten career receiving yards record of 3,788, and 247 from breaking it. Even his “quiet” game against Indiana helps his case. He finished with four catches for 68 yards, a season low, against a defense that clearly built their entire gameplan around him. What changes with a freshman quarterback There’s no point pretending this doesn’t change anything. Sayin and Smith had been playing together for two years, and that kind of timing doesn’t transfer overnight. Smith said after the game that it’s going to “take time” to build the same rapport with Luke Fahey. The bigger concern isn’t Smith’s talent, it’s volume. With a freshman under center and Ja’Kobi Jackson also out after surgery, Ohio State could lean a ton on Bo Jackson and the run game. Defenses could also bracket Smith even more aggressively, daring Fahey to beat them somewhere else. That could mean fewer 200 yard afternoons and more games like Indiana. The schedule doesn’t help either. Smith’s next three games will be at USC on Halloween, home against Oregon and home against Northwestern, followed by a road trip to Nebraska and Michigan to close the regular season. If Ohio State drops one or two of those games, it becomes much harder for any Buckeye to win the Heisman, because the award usually goes to the best player on a team that’s in the national title and top ten conversation. JULIAN SAYIN TO JEREMIAH SMITH GREATEST EVER OMFG pic.twitter.com/7sh3cbrlBY — wok (@wokdior) October 17, 2026 Why I still think he wins it But here’s the thing: Smith’s case doesn’t depend on Sayin the way a quarterback’s case depends on his receivers. Voters already believe he’s the best player in college football, and he’s spent three years reinforcing that belief. The only way that changes is if his production falls off a cliff or if someone like Mensah runs the table with a historic season. If anything, playing with a freshman quarterback gives Smith a chance to strengthen his case. If he keeps catching contested passes, keeps scoring touchdowns and keeps Ohio State winning while Fahey learns on the fly, voters will notice. It’s one thing to put up big numbers with a Heisman finalist throwing to you. It’s another to carry an offense through a quarterback injury in the middle of a playoff push. Wide receivers don’t win the Heisman often. Only a few have done it, with the most recent being DeVonta Smith in 2020. To get there, a receiver has to be clearly better than everyone else on the field, every week. Smith has been that player for three years. Smith doesn’t need perfect throws. He doesn’t even need to run the right route apparently. He just needs a chance to go and get the ball, and Ohio State’s job is to keep giving him that chance. If they do, I expect Smith to be in New York on Dec. 12, walking off the stage with the trophy.

item.title: Hometown Hero Who Caught Reds’ 1990 World Series Final Out Dies at 63
item.description: Todd Benzinger and his Cincinnati Reds teammates stand for the national anthem before a 1990 World Series game against the Oakland Athletics in Oakland, California. Getty The Cincinnati Reds are mourning the loss of a hometown World Series champion. Former Reds first baseman Todd Benzinger, who caught the final out of Cincinnati’s historic 1990 World Series championship, has died at the age of 63. The organization announced his passing on Thursday, October 22, remembering the former player for his contributions to one of the most celebrated teams in franchise history. For Cincinnati fans, Benzinger will forever be associated with the moment the Reds completed their stunning sweep of the Oakland Athletics. But his connection to the city extended well beyond that unforgettable play. Benzinger grew up in the Cincinnati area, attended New Richmond High School and eventually returned to professional baseball as a manager in the Reds’ minor league system. His passing marks the loss of a player who represented Cincinnati both on and off the field. Cincinnati Reds Announce Death of 1990 World Series Champion The Reds shared the news of Benzinger’s death on Thursday, paying tribute to their former first baseman and extending condolences to those close to him. In their announcement, the organization remembered Benzinger for his role in one of the most memorable chapters of Reds history. The Cincinnati Reds are saddened by the passing of former first baseman and 1990 World Series champion Todd Benzinger. Todd will be remembered with great affection and gratitude for his place in one of the most memorable chapters in Reds history. Our deepest condolences go out… pic.twitter.com/h3P6UWTNn1 — Cincinnati Reds (@Reds) October 22, 2026 Benzinger was born on February 11, 1963, in Dayton, Kentucky, just across the Ohio River from Cincinnati. He attended New Richmond High School in Ohio before being selected by the Boston Red Sox in the fourth round of the 1981 MLB Draft. He made his major league debut with Boston in 1987 and joined his hometown Reds ahead of the 1989 season. Benzinger quickly became a regular in Cincinnati’s lineup. In 1989, he appeared in 161 games, recording 154 hits, 17 home runs and 76 RBIs. 1990 would prove to be the most memorable of his career. Benzinger helped Cincinnati capture its first World Series Championship since 1976. Our deepest condolences go out… pic.twitter.com/h3P6UWTNn1 — Cincinnati Reds (@Reds) October 22, 2026 Benzinger was born on February 11, 1963, in Dayton, Kentucky, just across the Ohio River from Cincinnati. He attended New Richmond High School in Ohio before being selected by the Boston Red Sox in the fourth round of the 1981 MLB Draft. In 1989, he appeared in 161 games, recording 154 hits, 17 home runs and 76 RBIs. 1990 would prove to be the most memorable of his career. Benzinger helped Cincinnati capture its first World Series Championship since 1976. Todd Benzinger Caught Final Out of Reds’ 1990 World Series Victory The 1990 World Series remains one of the most celebrated moments in Cincinnati sports history. Despite entering the series against an Oakland Athletics team coming off three consecutive American League pennants, the Reds dominated the matchup. Cincinnati won the first three games and entered Game 4 in Oakland needing just one more victory to secure the championship. With the Reds leading 2-1 in the ninth inning, Oakland’s Carney Lansford came to the plate representing the Athletics’ final hope of extending the series. Lansford lifted a foul pop-up toward first base. Benzinger tracked the ball and made the catch, officially completing Cincinnati’s four-game sweep . Benzinger will always live on in Cincinnati history. He had strong connections to the area and made a key impact on youth baseball in the Cincinnati/Northern Kentucky area. The 1990 title remains Cincinnati’s most recent World Series championship. For generations of Reds fans, that catch is one of the defining images of the franchise’s modern history. The current iteration of the Cincinnati Reds has struggled to compete in recent years. They’re watching a former Red play in the World Series while they missed the postseason in 8 of the past 10 seasons. While the Reds have clear questions going into the offseason, right now all focus is on a hometown legend, a reminder of the greatness that the Cincinnati Reds can achieve. Rest in peace, Todd Benzinger. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Hometown Hero Who Caught Reds’ 1990 World Series Final Out Dies at 63 appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Doctor Warns Jalen Hurts Could Suffer Serious Bleeding if Tackled on Blood Thinners as NFLPA Calls for Investigation
item.description: Image Credit: lev radin / Shutterstock. Jalen Hurts could suffer serious bleeding from a tackle while taking blood thinners, Dr. David Abbasi warned during an October 20 appearance on TMZ's In The Know . The Philadelphia Eagles quarterback, 28, has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, or blood clots in both lungs. The diagnosis was announced October 19. In a joint statement , the Eagles and his agent, Nicole Lynn, described him as clinically stable, without significant functional limitations. They expect him to recover fully. Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, according to an Associated Press report citing a person familiar with the situation. Why Blood Thinners Make Head Injuries Especially Dangerous Anticoagulants reduce the blood's ability to form clots. That helps prevent existing clots from growing and new ones from developing, but it also makes bleeding after an injury harder to control. Dr. Jonathan Paul, director of UChicago Medicine's Pulmonary Embolism Response Team, identified head injuries as a particular concern because bleeding inside the brain can have catastrophic consequences. Paul, who has not treated Hurts, told PEOPLE that trauma involving the abdomen or limbs could also cause internal bleeding. His comments describe the risks associated with the medication; no bleeding complication has been announced in Hurts' case. Treatment Could Last Months, With No Return Date Announced Abbasi estimated that Hurts could be sidelined for three to six months, depending on his treatment and recovery. Under American Society of Hematology guidelines , decisions about continuing anticoagulation after the initial treatment course depend partly on whether a clot was associated with a temporary trigger, an ongoing risk factor or no identifiable cause. The Eagles and Lynn have ruled out contact activities during treatment. They anticipate that Hurts will have the opportunity to resume contact football after discontinuing blood thinners, but have not announced a date for his return. What Happened Before and After the London Game According to the Eagles' medical timeline , Hurts first sought treatment for his calf on October 8. He told staff that an opponent's cleat had struck his left calf during the October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. An ultrasound in London on October 10 found a superficial clot. The team's medical staff and London physicians reviewed the results and concluded he could safely play, with activity and mobility considered important. He faced the Jacksonville Jaguars on October 11 and returned to Philadelphia. A repeat ultrasound on October 14 showed movement in the clot, prompting further evaluation. Abbasi identified the calf injury and prolonged sitting during transatlantic travel as possible contributors. Those explanations remain unconfirmed; the Eagles have not announced a definitive cause. item.content:encoded: Image Credit: lev radin / Shutterstock. Jalen Hurts could suffer serious bleeding from a tackle while taking blood thinners, Dr. David Abbasi warned during an October 20 appearance on TMZ's In The Know . The Philadelphia Eagles quarterback, 28, has deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli, or blood clots in both lungs. The diagnosis was announced October 19. In a joint statement , the Eagles and his agent, Nicole Lynn, described him as clinically stable, without significant functional limitations. They expect him to recover fully. Hurts is expected to miss the rest of the 2026 season, according to an Associated Press report citing a person familiar with the situation. Why Blood Thinners Make Head Injuries Especially Dangerous Anticoagulants reduce the blood's ability to form clots. That helps prevent existing clots from growing and new ones from developing, but it also makes bleeding after an injury harder to control. Dr. Jonathan Paul, director of UChicago Medicine's Pulmonary Embolism Response Team, identified head injuries as a particular concern because bleeding inside the brain can have catastrophic consequences. Paul, who has not treated Hurts, told PEOPLE that trauma involving the abdomen or limbs could also cause internal bleeding. His comments describe the risks associated with the medication; no bleeding complication has been announced in Hurts' case. Treatment Could Last Months, With No Return Date Announced Abbasi estimated that Hurts could be sidelined for three to six months, depending on his treatment and recovery. Under American Society of Hematology guidelines , decisions about continuing anticoagulation after the initial treatment course depend partly on whether a clot was associated with a temporary trigger, an ongoing risk factor or no identifiable cause. The Eagles and Lynn have ruled out contact activities during treatment. They anticipate that Hurts will have the opportunity to resume contact football after discontinuing blood thinners, but have not announced a date for his return. What Happened Before and After the London Game According to the Eagles' medical timeline , Hurts first sought treatment for his calf on October 8. He told staff that an opponent's cleat had struck his left calf during the October 4 game against the Los Angeles Rams. An ultrasound in London on October 10 found a superficial clot. The team's medical staff and London physicians reviewed the results and concluded he could safely play, with activity and mobility considered important. He faced the Jacksonville Jaguars on October 11 and returned to Philadelphia. A repeat ultrasound on October 14 showed movement in the clot, prompting further evaluation. Abbasi identified the calf injury and prolonged sitting during transatlantic travel as possible contributors. Those explanations remain unconfirmed; the Eagles have not announced a definitive cause. NFLPA Calls for an Investigation Into Hurts' Care https://t.co/wZyVLPcXvD — NFLPA (@NFLPA) October 21, 2026 The NFL Players Association said October 20 that the league had told it no review was planned. The union called for a full investigation before conclusions were drawn, emphasizing the need to establish the facts and protect players. NFL chief medical officer Dr. Allen Sills defended the Eagles' staff. He said a worsening outcome did not necessarily establish that earlier medical decisions had been improper. "We welcome that," Commissioner Roger Goodell said October 21, according to Reuters , while maintaining that medical protocols had been followed. The NFL has not announced disciplinary action against Philadelphia. Hurts Can Continue Conditioning and Help His Teammates The Eagles and Lynn said Hurts can remain around the team and continue conditioning while receiving treatment. Head coach Nick Sirianni has deferred medical questions to physicians but offered a personal response to his quarterback's absence: "I miss him," he said, according to NFL.com . Wide receiver Britain Covey had said on October 15 that Hurts was discussing offensive adjustments with teammates and looking for ways to get the unit going.

item.title: ESPN proposes a 49ers-Colts trade
item.description: (Photo by Justin Casterline/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are undefeated and sit atop the NFC. In an interview last week, general manager John Lynch joked about how the team was connected to every player on the trade market. The 49ers could stand to add depth at defensive tackle. You can never have enough pass rushers, so any defensive lineman would be a welcome addition. Here’s ESPN’s Bill Barnwell’s excerpt from one of his trade proposals in today’s article: San Francisco fans are understandably dreaming about a reunion with DeForest Buckner , who was once dealt in the opposite direction between these two teams for a first-round pick, but I’m not sure that’s as great of a fit as it might seem. The 49ers already have Osa Odighizuwa playing in that penetrating defensive tackle role, and rookie Gracen Halton has flashed alongside him, with sacks in each of the past two games. Buckner is still a great player, and I wouldn’t fault the 49ers for just lining up as many superstars up front as possible and daring opposing offensive lines to simply figure it out, but this team really needs more help at nose tackle. San Francisco is 27th in success rate against the run so far this season. A year ago, it was 31st. The 49ers have been able to insulate themselves against run game issues by playing from ahead for most of the season, but they’ll need to be better against the run by the postseason. Adding Stewart to the defensive line rotation would go a long way in helping San Francisco plug up those run game woes. The 33-year-old is a useful player and in the final year of his deal, but his contract is also expensive; he’s owed $8.2 million in cash over the remainder of the season. The 49ers don’t have cap concerns after restructuring some of their more significant deals, but that’s a big cash outlay. They could encourage the Colts to absorb more of the money by offering a better draft pick, but with the 49ers still undefeated and fielding one of the oldest cores in football, I’d push ownership to spend now to try to build a team that can win a title. Stewart isn’t the most exciting addition, but he’s the sort of player the Niners need. Sidebar: Right underneath it, Barnwell has the Rams trading for…a kicker. For what it’s worth, Sumer Sports has the 49ers 16th in rushing success rate. RBSDM has them 14th. If you filter it down to success rate against running backs, you still get 16th. So the defense is league average no matter how you split it. That doesn’t change the point of adding a nose tackle. I’d still push back, though. Raheem Morris is thriving with athletes up front. They are winning with quickness and are always on the move. The 5-down fronts help, too. For a seventh-rounder, sure. But, in my opinion, not having “space eaters” who aren’t agile, like Alfred Collins and CJ West, has quietly benefited the defensive line. They are covering more ground and causing more chaos. With a body type like Stewart, you’re unlikely to yield

item.title: FIFA begins formal bidding process for U.S. broadcast rights to 2030 World Cup
item.description: Credit: REUTERS/John Sibley We’ll soon know which broadcaster (or broadcasters) will secure rights to the 2030 FIFA World Cup in the United States. FIFA has formally opened the bidding process for U.S. broadcast rights to the 2030 World Cup, according to multiple reports on Thursday. The process will allow broadcasters to submit bids for the 2030 tournament, along with the 2034 tournament if they choose to do so. FIFA is reportedly open to selling the 2030 tournament as a standalone event, or have it bundled with the 2034 tournament. The 2030 World Cup is scheduled to take place in Spain, Morocco, and Portugal after opening matches in Uruguay, Argentina, and Paraguay. The 2034 World Cup is scheduled to take place entirely in Saudi Arabia. As was previously reported, FIFA prefers to bundle its English- and Spanish-language U.S. broadcast rights together for the 2030 tournament. When Fox held English-language rights and NBC’s Telemundo held Spanish-language rights to this summer’s World Cup, there was a level of angst from Fox that Telemundo and NBC-owned Peacock were cutting into its potential audience. As it turned out, there were a significant number of English speakers choosing to watch on Telemundo or Peacock , either for accessibility reasons or simply out of preference. Bundling the rights together solves this issue. Per CNBC , FIFA is open to offers that come from just a single media company, or a joint offer from multiple companies, “potentially between a streamer and a traditional broadcaster.” Should rights be sold to a streamer, precedent would suggest the streamer will have to sublicense at least a portion of games to a traditional broadcaster, or make a set number of games available in front of a paywall. Netflix, for instance, just won rights to broadcast the 2030 tournament in Spain, but the deal ensures at least one match per day airs on a traditional broadcaster, as well as all matches featuring Spain, and the semifinals and final. Bids are due by Nov. 19, according to Sports Business Journal , at which point FIFA will send a contingent of representatives to the U.S. and either narrow the field or choose a winner. FIFA intends to choose its next World Cup partner before the end of the year. Numerous media companies are reportedly interested in securing rights , including incumbents Fox and NBC. ESPN has also said it is interested in bidding, and Netflix figures to be heavily involved considering it recent deal in Spain along with already holding rights to the 2027 and 2031 women’s tournaments. Amazon’s Prime Video has also indicated interest in the event. Others like YouTube or Apple could potentially kick the tires as well. The post FIFA begins formal bidding process for U.S. broadcast rights to 2030 World Cup appeared first on Awful Announcing .

item.title: Montreal Canadiens Receive Tough Nick Suzuki News Before Blackhawks Game
item.description: WASHINGTON, DC - OCTOBER 14: Nick Suzuki #14 of the Montreal Canadiens looks on after scoring a goal against the Washington Capitals during the third period at Capital One Arena on October 14, 2026 in Washington, DC. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) Getty MONTREAL, CANADA - OCTOBER 17: Cole Caufield #13 of the Montréal Canadiens celebrates his goal with teammates Juraj Slafkovský #20 and Nick Suzuki #14 during the first period against the Buffalo Sabres at the Bell Centre on October 17, 2026 in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. (Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images) Getty The Montreal Canadiens are off to a decent start to the 2026-27 campaign. Across nine games played thus far, the Habs are 4-3-2, which is good for 6th in the Atlantic Division, which is shaping up to be very tough this season. Montreal’s next game is an away clash with the Chicago Blackhawks. Before the Blackhawks contest (on Friday), a very notable Nick Suzuki injury update emerged. More NHL on Heavy: Carolina Hurricanes Quietly Make 3 Roster Announcements Ahead of Oilers Clash Nick Suzuki Expected to Miss 2-4 Weeks with Injury Getty MONTREAL, CANADA – OCTOBER 17: Cole Caufield #13 of the Montréal Canadiens celebrates his goal with teammates Juraj Slafkovský #20 and Nick Suzuki #14 during the first period against the Buffalo Sabres at the Bell Centre on October 17, 2026 in Montreal, Quebec, Canada. (Photo by Minas Panagiotakis/Getty Images) Per a team announcement, star center Nick Suzuki is expected to miss 2-4 weeks with an upper-body injury. ProHockeyRumors.com’s Bradley Keith wrote (about Suzuki): “Breaking out last season with 101 points as a bonafide superstar, the 27-year-old has continued that pace into this season with 12 points in nine games. Few can impact the game in as many areas as he can, leading both the power play and penalty kill, logging heavy minutes at 21:47, fifth most in the NHL out of forwards. With high expectations, his Habs have come out of the gate a bit slower than hoped with a 4-3-2 record. The group has struggled to keep the puck out of the net, allowing the ninth most goals at this point.” Owen Beck is the corresponding move for the Habs, as he’s being recalled from AHL Laval. It’s a pretty tough blow for the Canadiens, as Keith notes, Suzuki is the clear heartbeat for Montreal that makes the first line work in unison, and he’s been the leader of one of the NHL’s most feared power play units for the past couple of seasons. The hope is that he’ll be able to return within the 2-4 week timeframe, but there will certainly be more updates to come. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Montreal Canadiens Receive Tough Nick Suzuki News Before Blackhawks Game appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Bearman Welcomes Câmara to F1, Sets Sights on Team Leadership
item.description: Oliver Bearman at the Goodwood Festival of Speed. (Photo: Johnny Rogers/FanAmp) AUSTIN, Texas — Haas arrive at Austin in the wake of announcing that Rafael Câmara will replace Esteban Ocon in 2027. The Brazilian youngster won the Formula 3 championship last season and currently leads the Formula 2 standings with just two races to go. On Thursday, Oliver Bearman spoke to the media, including FanAmp, about the similarities he shares with his new teammate and his enthusiasm to become the lead driver next season. Bearman noted the two Ferrari juniors share many things in common, including a birthday week. “It's funny because we joined Ferrari on the same day. We both signed at the same time, and I think we're like 3 or 4 days apart in, in birthdays, so we have a joint birthday party.” Ahead of Câmara’s rookie season, Bearman lauded the nurturing atmosphere at Haas, saying, “I think Haas is a great place to start your F1 career. It's a great team, welcoming, and probably quite different compared to other teams.” After racing alongside Esteban Ocon, a ten-year veteran of the sport, Bearman feels he is ready to become the lead driver for the American outfit. Speaking to his readiness to mentor a rookie teammate, Bearman said, “I think this year has been a big step for myself in terms of on-track performance, but more importantly, how I deal with the team, how I transition into that role of leading the team. I think I've seen a big step in how I deal with the team, but also how the team values my input and my feedback.” Despite Bearman’s enthusiasm to welcome a new teammate in 2027, Haas still haven’t confirmed his seat for next season. Bearman remained steadfast about his intent to stay at Haas, with an eye toward challenging at the top of the grid. “In terms of a midfield team, Haas is the team that I want to be with and I see my future with, but at some point as well I feel like I've earned the opportunity to go out and look for a top-4 team. And of course, with my link with Ferrari, that would be my ultimate goal.” Bearman enters the weekend thirteenth in the World Drivers’ Championship with 23 points. He looks to build from an encouraging performance at Circuit of the Americas last season, when he finished P9.

item.title: With the Title in Sight, Antonelli Remains Focused
item.description: Kimi Antonelli at the 2026 United States Grand Prix. (Photo: Greg Kallman/FanAmp) AUSTIN, Texas — Entering this weekend, Kimi Antonelli leads the World Drivers’ Championship by 102 points and can mathematically clinch the title on Sunday. Antonelli would become the youngest champion in Formula 1 history, breaking the previous record held by Sebastian Vettel by over three years. On Thursday, Antonelli told the media, including FanAmp, that he remains focused on the task at hand. When asked about what he thinks about being so close to winning the championship, Antonelli said, "Just always the same mindset as I had all year, one race at a time, just try to do the best I can every week." In a joint interview session that also included seven-time champion, Lewis Hamilton, Antonelli shared how important it was to follow the F1 legend by winning a title at Mercedes. "It was a dream, it's something I've dreamt of since I was little." Before unpacking his excitement any further, though, Antonelli returned his focus to Sunday. "But at the same time I need to keep going, keep pushing. It's not over yet, so first we're trying to finish the job properly." To seal his maiden championship in Austin, the Italian youngster must win the Grand Prix, with teammate George Russell finishing ninth or lower, and Lewis Hamilton finishing fifth or lower. With betting lines currently predicting both Russell and Hamilton to reach the top 5, this scenario is a long shot. Another route to victory, however, could come in the form of a shortened championship. A recent missile strike Dhahran, nearly 100 miles from the Lusail International circuit in Qatar, sowed doubts that the final two races of the season will continue as scheduled. Formula 1 reportedly made preparations for Imola to host aseason finale if security concerns in the Middle East force the cancellation of the Qatar and Abu Dhabi Grands Prix. In this scenario, Antonelli can clinch the title by winning the Grand Prix this weekend. Even if he finishes among the top 5, he can still win the championship by finishing ahead of Russell if Hamilton does not win the race.

Chicago is riding a bounce-back 31-23 road win over Atlanta, with Caleb Williams looking sharp in his return (30 of 36 for 305 yards and a touchdown). item.title: Rodri’s Barcelona benching raises fresh questions after PSG deliver a Champions League blow
item.description: Source: canno73/Depositphotos Some nights in football can change the mood around a whole club. One team arrives full of confidence and leaves with doubts. Barcelona felt that shift this week, and the debate has not stopped yet. The story centers on Rodri and a single missing name on a team sheet. It sounds quite small. Yet in modern football, one decision can ripple through tactics, fan opinion, and long-term plans. The night Barcelona lost its anchor PSG beat Barcelona 4-2 in Paris on Tuesday. Rodri had played 172 of Barcelona’s first 180 Champions League minutes before that night. The defeat was Barcelona’s first dropped points in Europe this season after victories in their opening 2 league-phase matches. Rodri has quickly become an important presence in Barcelona’s midfield. Against PSG, Marc Bernal started in his place, and Rodri did not enter until the 60th minute with Barcelona still searching for greater control in the middle. His absence from the starting XI immediately raised questions because he had been one of Barcelona’s most-used midfielders. Reports before kickoff pointed to workload management and muscular fatigue rather than a serious injury. Why Rodri started on the bench Rodri was named among Barcelona’s substitutes against PSG after carrying a heavy workload for club and country. Hansi Flick said before kickoff that he wanted to protect the midfielder from overload after Rodri had played the previous 3 matches. Earlier reports said Rodri had been dealing with muscular fatigue and had not looked at his best in training. The issue was described as minor rather than a serious injury, which allowed Barcelona to keep him available from the bench. Barcelona also traveled with defensive shortages. Eric Garcia, Jules Koundé and Andreas Christensen were unavailable, and Rodri was considered one possible emergency option if Flick needed additional cover during the match. Source: operations@newsimages.co.uk/Depositphotos Flick explains his rotation decision Hansi Flick explained the decision before kickoff. He said Barcelona needed to protect its players from overload and noted that Rodri had played the previous 3 matches, making PSG the midfielder’s fourth match in a demanding run. Flick stressed that Barcelona trusted Marc Bernal to step into the midfield. The decision came with El Clásico against Real Madrid only 5 days away and reports that Rodri had also been managing minor muscular fatigue. item.content:encoded: Source: canno73/Depositphotos Some nights in football can change the mood around a whole club. One team arrives full of confidence and leaves with doubts. Barcelona felt that shift this week, and the debate has not stopped yet. The story centers on Rodri and a single missing name on a team sheet. It sounds quite small. Yet in modern football, one decision can ripple through tactics, fan opinion, and long-term plans. The night Barcelona lost its anchor PSG beat Barcelona 4-2 in Paris on Tuesday. Rodri had played 172 of Barcelona’s first 180 Champions League minutes before that night. The defeat was Barcelona’s first dropped points in Europe this season after victories in their opening 2 league-phase matches. Rodri has quickly become an important presence in Barcelona’s midfield. Against PSG, Marc Bernal started in his place, and Rodri did not enter until the 60th minute with Barcelona still searching for greater control in the middle. His absence from the starting XI immediately raised questions because he had been one of Barcelona’s most-used midfielders. Reports before kickoff pointed to workload management and muscular fatigue rather than a serious injury. Why Rodri started on the bench Rodri was named among Barcelona’s substitutes against PSG after carrying a heavy workload for club and country. Hansi Flick said before kickoff that he wanted to protect the midfielder from overload after Rodri had played the previous 3 matches. Earlier reports said Rodri had been dealing with muscular fatigue and had not looked at his best in training. The issue was described as minor rather than a serious injury, which allowed Barcelona to keep him available from the bench. Barcelona also traveled with defensive shortages. Eric Garcia, Jules Koundé and Andreas Christensen were unavailable, and Rodri was considered one possible emergency option if Flick needed additional cover during the match. Source: operations@newsimages.co.uk/Depositphotos Flick explains his rotation decision Hansi Flick explained the decision before kickoff. He said Barcelona needed to protect its players from overload and noted that Rodri had played the previous 3 matches, making PSG the midfielder’s fourth match in a demanding run. Flick stressed that Barcelona trusted Marc Bernal to step into the midfield. The decision came with El Clásico against Real Madrid only 5 days away and reports that Rodri had also been managing minor muscular fatigue. The timing nevertheless invited debate because PSG entered the match as the reigning European champions. Barcelona ultimately lost 4-2, with Rodri coming on for Bernal in the 60th minute. What a midfield anchor really does A defensive midfielder sits in front of the back line. He wins loose balls and breaks up dangerous attacks. He also gives teammates a safe passing option whenever a hard press squeezes the pitch tightly. That role looks simple, but it is not. The player must read danger before it appears and then act quickly. Rodri is widely admired for exactly this skill, and his teammates clearly lean on it. Think of him as a quiet traffic controller. When he plays, the cars usually move very smoothly. When he sits out, even small mistakes cause long delays, and Barcelona felt the whole jam right away. Bernal steps into massive shoes Marc Bernal took Rodri’s place in Hansi Flick’s starting lineup. Barcelona arrived in France after winning all 11 of their games this season. That perfect run made the change feel even more striking to onlookers. Bernal is a young midfielder with real promise and a bright future. Yet replacing Rodri is a truly huge ask for anyone. Few players in world football read the game with such calm and control. Replacement stories are always risky because the standards are so high in elite football. Fans compare every touch with a proven star. That pressure can freeze a young player or push him to grow overnight. Rodri’s fast start in Catalonia Rodri scored his first goal for Barcelona since arriving this summer. It arrived just days before the demanding trip to face PSG. The strike confirmed just how quickly he has settled into Hansi Flick’s system. A new league and a new club bring fresh challenges. La Liga demands patience and sharp positioning against teams that sit deep. Rodri’s calm style suits that task, and he adapts quickly to each opponent. Settling in at a new club is one thing. Carrying a title challenge on your shoulders is another. Rodri now has to prove he can guide Barcelona through the biggest nights without needing regular rest. Little-known fact: Rodri became the first Manchester City player to win the Ballon d’Or when he took the award in 2024. He was also the first Spanish men’s winner since Luis Suárez in 1960. Source: operations@newsimages.co.uk/Depositphotos El Clásico looms over everything now Barcelona host Real Madrid at Camp Nou on Sunday, October 25, at 9 p.m. local time. The league confirmed the date and time long ago. The fixture lands only five days after the PSG loss. The stakes for both sides are plain to see. A win would restore confidence and silence doubts raised in Paris. A slip would add pressure on a squad that had looked flawless only days earlier. Flick has handled this fierce rivalry quite well. He has beaten Real Madrid six times in seven meetings across all competitions since taking charge. Yet this time he must solve a tricky midfield puzzle first. What this loss reveals about depth Great teams survive injuries and rotation without losing their identity or confidence. That is the real test of squad depth at the top. One missing piece should bend a plan but never break it completely. Depth also means trust in young players from the club’s own academy. La Masia keeps producing talents who can step into big matches. That pipeline is a major strength, and it needs constant careful protection. Still, academy graduates cannot replace every veteran skill overnight or without mistakes. Experience in controlling tempo comes from years of high-level football. Barcelona must decide how to blend both groups in the weeks ahead. TL;DR PSG beat Barcelona 4-2 while Rodri sat on the bench. Reports said Rodri was rested for fatigue and was not seriously hurt. Hansi Flick said he rotated to protect Rodri from overload. Marc Bernal filled the gap, and Barcelona looked less settled without their anchor. El Clásico against Real Madrid arrives on October 25 at Camp Nou. This article was made with AI assistance and human editing. item.description: Gary A. Vasquez-USA TODAY Sports. 3 reasons Rays don’t stand a chance in World Series vs. Brewers appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Rays have earned respect throughout October. The Milwaukee Brewers should still be the team celebrating when the 2026 World Series ends. Game 1 begins Friday at American Family Field, where the Rays face an opponent built to punish mistakes that decide postseason games. The Brewers’ advantages extend from their bullpen to the bottom of their lineup, with home field providing another obstacle. The Rays can win individual matchups . Across a series, however, the Brewers have the stronger combination of depth, sustained production, and favorable circumstances. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Brewers’ bullpen leaves Rays little margin for error The Brewers can turn an early lead into a succession of difficult pitching matchups. Their relievers have a 1.33 postseason ERA, backed by power arms and effective secondary pitches. That combination presents a challenge. The Rays must handle premium velocity while also protecting against secondary pitches. Aaron Ashby adds another complication. He has delivered 12 1/3 scoreless postseason innings, allowing Pat Murphy to seek multiple innings from one trusted reliever. Driving a starter from the game therefore does not necessarily give the Rays a softer assignment. It can bring them directly into Milwaukee’s greatest strength. The Rays’ bullpen deserves credit, and a lower radar reading does not mean inferior pitching. Milwaukee’s advantage lies in its range of reliable high-leverage options. If the Rays waste scoring opportunities, the Brewers can keep changing the challenge without asking one pitcher to cover every important inning. That makes sustained comebacks a demanding route to victory. Milwaukee’s deeper lineup can wear down Tampa Bay The Rays cannot build their pitching plan around stopping only Milwaukee’s most recognizable hitters. The Brewers got more production from the sixth through ninth spots in their lineup during the second half than the Rays did. Drew Rasmussen and Freddy Peralta can suppress that offense. But a lineup producing throughout the order offers fewer opportunities to recover from an exhausting inning. That depth can wear down opposing pitchers. A walk near the bottom can create another plate appearance for a dangerous hitter at the top. A prolonged battle can push a starter closer to his workload limit. Jake Bauers supplied examples against the Los Angeles Dodgers. He drew a 12-pitch walk in NLCS Game 2 and homered after 11 pitches in Game 3. Those outcomes cannot be guaranteed against Tampa Bay. They do illustrate how Milwaukee can force repeated execution before an inning ends. The Rays need efficient starts to limit their bullpen’s exposure. The Rays’ bullpen deserves credit, and a lower radar reading does not mean inferior pitching. Milwaukee’s advantage lies in its range of reliable high-leverage options. If the Rays waste scoring opportunities, the Brewers can keep changing the challenge without asking one pitcher to cover every important inning. That makes sustained comebacks a demanding route to victory. The Brewers got more production from the sixth through ninth spots in their lineup during the second half than the Rays did. Drew Rasmussen and Freddy Peralta can suppress that offense. But a lineup producing throughout the order offers fewer opportunities to recover from an exhausting inning. That depth can wear down opposing pitchers. A walk near the bottom can create another plate appearance for a dangerous hitter at the top. A prolonged battle can push a starter closer to his workload limit. Jake Bauers supplied examples against the Los Angeles Dodgers. He drew a 12-pitch walk in NLCS Game 2 and homered after 11 pitches in Game 3. Those outcomes cannot be guaranteed against Tampa Bay. They do illustrate how Milwaukee can force repeated execution before an inning ends. The Rays need efficient starts to limit their bullpen’s exposure. The Brewers have the offensive depth to make that efficiency difficult to sustain. Brewers’ season-long edge comes with home field The Brewers finished 103-59 with a +214 run differential. Tampa Bay finished 98-64 with a +86 differential. The five-win difference tells only part of the story. The much larger scoring margin strengthens the case that Milwaukee’s superiority extends beyond its impressive October results. Run differential cannot settle a short series, but it provides a broader foundation for this argument than momentum alone. The Brewers also hold home-field advantage. Both teams finished 55-26 at home, making Milwaukee’s right to host four potential games meaningful. That creates a straightforward requirement for the Rays. Even if the Rays protect their own ballpark, they must win at least once in Milwaukee. A potential Game 7 would also take place in Milwaukee. The Brewers open the series with two opportunities to establish control at home. Rasmussen, Peralta, and Tampa Bay’s leading hitters give the club ways to challenge these advantages. The stronger foundation still belongs to the Brewers. Milwaukee can make Tampa Bay work for runs, extend scoring opportunities and apply pressure at home. The Rays must overcome those challenges often enough to win four games. The Brewers have the depth to keep presenting them, even when one pitcher struggles or a key hitter goes quiet. That leaves the Rays facing the tougher path to a championship. item.title: IndyCar set to drop Nashville Superspeedway and D.C. for 2027; Barcelona announcement looms
item.description: Motorsport photo The IndyCar Series is shaking up its calendar for the 2027 season, with Motorsport.com learning that the championship will not return to the Nashville Superspeedway, nor will it stage an encore event for the wildly successful Freedom 250 Grand Prix on the streets of Washington, D.C.. However, North America’s premier open-wheel championship is simultaneously expanding its international footprint, having reached an agreement to race at Spain's Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya. Tennessee Presence in Jeopardy IndyCar has raced on the 1.33-mile D-shaped concrete oval in Lebanon, Tennessee, since 2024. That move followed a popular three-year stint on the downtown streets of Nashville for the Music City Grand Prix. The shift to the superspeedway was enacted as a temporary fix driven by extensive construction surrounding the Tennessee Titans' new NFL stadium, which stripped away vital footprint space required for team paddocks, transporters, and fan activations. While organizers and local leaders initially eyed a potential return to the downtown layout once the stadium project neared completion, the latest updates indicate IndyCar will lack a points-paying presence in the Volunteer State altogether for 2027. D.C. Success Won't Translate to a 2027 Return Despite massive fanfare, the inaugural Freedom 250 Grand Prix – conceived as a one-off celebration around The National Mall – will not see a 2027 encore. The unique 1.7-mile, seven-turn temporary street circuit turned heads across the sports world, drawing a staggering weekend crowd of over 215,000 spectators across the two-day show. Broadcast nationally on FOX, the race pulled in an average of 3.282 million viewers, cementing it as the most-watched non-Indy 500 IndyCar race since the open-wheel unification of 2008. Despite the blockbuster metrics, logistical realities have grounded plans for an immediate repeat. Heading to Spain While domestic stalwarts drop off, IndyCar is planting a major flag abroad. Motorsport.com has confirmed that Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya has finalized a multi-year deal to host an IndyCar round starting in the summer of 2027 . Slated tentatively for July 18, the event brings premier North American open-wheel racing directly to the home country of five-time series champion Alex Palou . An official announcement from series leadership, with Palou and IndyCar CEO Mark Miles in on-hand, is expected this Friday alongside the release of the remaining second-half schedule for the 2027 season. item.title: Warriors overreactions: Dubs are totally screwed no matter what Stephen Curry does this season
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Warriors overreactions: Dubs are totally screwed no matter what Stephen Curry does this season appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . On Wednesday evening, the Golden State Warriors stumbled out of the gates with an ugly loss to the Los Angeles Lakers on the road on opening night. The Warriors managed to stick around in the first half of this one, but ultimately fell apart in the third quarter and ended up losing by a final score of 127-105. Here are two overreactions from the loss. The Warriors will be bad this season This isn’t exactly a hot take, considering that few pundits have the Warriors making the playoffs this year. However, it was truly jarring to see just how little help Stephen Curry had on Wednesday, with the franchise icon scoring 16 points in the first quarter alone but not getting much support from anywhere else. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Of course, Brandin Podziemski being out didn’t help, and he should be back sooner rather than later. The team was also without big man Kristaps Porzingis, but it’s not exactly reasonable to project him being out on the floor consistently, considering his injury history and the fact that Golden State is now reportedly looking to trade him. Jimmy Butler will theoretically come back at some point this season, but the Warriors’ campaign could be fully behind the eight-ball by the time that happens. Overall, there wasn’t much to be encouraged about in Wednesday’s loss. Yaxel Lendeborg is the real deal One of the few sources of energy for Golden State in this one was rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who scored 12 points in the loss and also provided some intensity on the defensive end of the floor. Lendeborg found himself in an ongoing trash-talk feud with Lakers star Luka Doncic, a battle that Doncic won when he sent a half-court shot through the net just before the end of the second quarter. However, it certainly says something about the rookie that he was willing to talk smack to one of the game’s greatest players in his first-ever NBA contest, and he largely performed well, on offense, at least, in his own right. That kind of energy might be just what Golden State needs to keep their morale amid what could be an ugly season. Related: Stephen A. item.title: 4 Knicks Keys To Victory For Friday’s Matchup Versus Celtics
item.description: Oct 20, 2026; New York, New York, USA; New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson (11) reacts during the first quarter against the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Benjamin Yu, Editor After falling in their season opener on Tuesday, the New York Knicks will travel to TD Garden to play the Boston Celtics on Friday. Boston lost their season opener in Detroit on Tuesday, so both of these preseason top Eastern Conference teams will be vying for their first win of the campaign. Here are four things to keep an eye out for when watching this matchup. Contain Mitchell Robinson On The Glass Celtics center Mitchell Robinson will be playing in his first game against the Knicks in his career Friday. Robinson spent all eight previous seasons in his career with New York, and was one of the few players the team was unable to bring back after the championship run. Robinson is known especially for his offensive rebounding prowess, something that helped the Knicks greatly during their championship run. Robinson averaged 4.2 offensive rebounds per game in his 60 regular season appearances for the Knicks last season. The Knicks still have really good rebounding centers in Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond , but Robinson poses a new challenge on the glass for New York. Robinson has always been a force on the glass for the Knicks, and now it’s time for Towns and Drummond to limit the potential damage he can do in his revenge game. Robinson had a minor ankle injury in Boston’s season opener, but Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla said that he’ll be able to play Friday. The Knicks’ Starting 5 Need To Bounce Back Offensively In the Knicks’ season opener on Tuesday night, New York’s starting five did not have a particularly strong outing. Jalen Brunson was uncharacteristically missing shots he normally makes down the stretch, Towns got into foul trouble very early again, and OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges went missing for vast stretches of the game. While Josh Hart had a decent outing, it’s not an ideal strategy to win for Hart to be one of the top two players for the Knicks with the basketball. In order for the Knicks to win on Friday, Brunson has to be more efficient putting the ball into the net. Brunson in particular only made six of his 19 attempts from the field versus Philadelphia, and only attempted three shots beyond the arc. Eight of his 21 points came from the free-throw line, which is just not a recipe for winning basketball for the defending champions. item.content:encoded: Oct 20, 2026; New York, New York, USA; New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson (11) reacts during the first quarter against the Philadelphia 76ers at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Benjamin Yu, Editor After falling in their season opener on Tuesday, the New York Knicks will travel to TD Garden to play the Boston Celtics on Friday. Boston lost their season opener in Detroit on Tuesday, so both of these preseason top Eastern Conference teams will be vying for their first win of the campaign. Here are four things to keep an eye out for when watching this matchup. Contain Mitchell Robinson On The Glass Celtics center Mitchell Robinson will be playing in his first game against the Knicks in his career Friday. Robinson spent all eight previous seasons in his career with New York, and was one of the few players the team was unable to bring back after the championship run. Robinson is known especially for his offensive rebounding prowess, something that helped the Knicks greatly during their championship run. Robinson averaged 4.2 offensive rebounds per game in his 60 regular season appearances for the Knicks last season. The Knicks still have really good rebounding centers in Karl-Anthony Towns and Andre Drummond , but Robinson poses a new challenge on the glass for New York. Robinson has always been a force on the glass for the Knicks, and now it’s time for Towns and Drummond to limit the potential damage he can do in his revenge game. Robinson had a minor ankle injury in Boston’s season opener, but Celtics head coach Joe Mazzulla said that he’ll be able to play Friday. The Knicks’ Starting 5 Need To Bounce Back Offensively In the Knicks’ season opener on Tuesday night, New York’s starting five did not have a particularly strong outing. Jalen Brunson was uncharacteristically missing shots he normally makes down the stretch, Towns got into foul trouble very early again, and OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges went missing for vast stretches of the game. While Josh Hart had a decent outing, it’s not an ideal strategy to win for Hart to be one of the top two players for the Knicks with the basketball. In order for the Knicks to win on Friday, Brunson has to be more efficient putting the ball into the net. Brunson in particular only made six of his 19 attempts from the field versus Philadelphia, and only attempted three shots beyond the arc. Eight of his 21 points came from the free-throw line, which is just not a recipe for winning basketball for the defending champions. KAT Can’t Get Into Foul Trouble Oct 20, 2026; New York, New York, USA; New York Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns (32) shoots a three point shot against the Philadelphia 76ers during the fourth quarter at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images One of the biggest hindrances to the Knicks’ ability to produce offensively is Towns’ propensity to get into foul trouble. Due to three first-half fouls, Towns was only able to play 24 minutes on Tuesday night. Towns was the most efficient scorer in the starting lineup, shooting 6-9 from the field and 3-4 from beyond the arc, and losing your most efficient scorer on a given night for half the game is always a massive disadvantage. Towns’ ability to shoot from three is an ability that seldom centers are able to offer, which creates floor spacing that can pull rim protectors out to the arc and allow for easier opportunities inside the paint. Joel Embiid looked better defensively on Tuesday night than he has in years, in part because he wasn’t tasked with defending on the perimeter as much with Drummond’s extended minutes. In Friday’s game, the Knicks really need to be able to stretch the floor and pull Robinson out of the paint, where he thrives as a great rebounder and rim protector. However, the Knicks won’t be able to utilize Towns’ unique skill set with him on the bench, so it’s imperative that he limits the reckless fouls that he so often finds himself committing. The Knicks Must Prioritize Perimeter Defense Since Mazzulla took over as Boston’s head coach, the Celtics’ identity offensively has centered around their three-point shooting. Boston has finished in the top five of three-point attempts in all of Mazzulla’s four seasons as head coach, including having the most attempts in 2023-24 and 2024-25. This trend looks to continue this season as well, as Boston attempted 42 shots beyond the arc on Tuesday. The Celtics have a plethora of threats from three, including Jayson Tatum , Derrick White , Payton Pritchard , and Paul George , who went 7-12 from three in his debut for Boston on Tuesday. To combat any three-point barrages, the Knicks must prioritize defending the three-point line. Anunoby and Bridges are regarded as two of the best wing defenders in the league, and Hart is also no slouch defensively. With Robinson not being a threat from three by any means, New York will consistently have someone there in the paint to battle Robinson for rebounds on missed shots. It’s crucial that the other four Knicks defenders keep Boston from hitting their threes left and right on them over the course of 48 minutes. item.title: Ben Kohles climbs leaderboard in Bermuda behind run of six straight birdies
item.description: Despite posting birdies on eight of his 10 opening holes, Ben Kohles trailed Ben Silverman in Bermuda with two left to play during Thursday's opening round. The duo now carries a share of the clubhouse lead with Danny Walker at 8 under after Kohles birdied the par-5 17th which was good for his 11th circle on the day. Silverman carded a bogey-free 63 at Port Royal Golf Course. Kohles' first 18 holes were not nearly as clean. While any round with double-digit birdies is a massive success, Kohles did give three shots back — one at the par-4 fourth hole that went on to kick-start a spree of six straight birdies at Nos. 5-10. He bogeyed another par-4 — the 383-yard 12th — on his back nine before missing a par putt at No. 16 for his final blemish of the day. Every shot matters a little extra this fall for the 36-year-old Kohles , who sits tied with a one-shot lead over Jonathan Byrd, Chan Kim and Mackenzie Hughes after signing his 63. Kohles was at a crossroads when he opted for the PGA Tour's inaugural Biltmore Championship last month. He sat 17th on the Korn Ferry Tour points list when he made the decision to bet on himself — in an attempt to stay inside the top 100 on the FedExCup points list. He is No. 80 after a trio of finishes inside the top 20. Kohles placed T-15 in North Carolina, T-13 at the Bank of Utah Championship and T-17 at the Baycurrent Classic in Japan two weeks ago. “I looked it at like, I could play the last three Korn Ferry events and miss the first three in the fall and lock up my card. At the same time, I’ve been doing this long enough,” Kohles said with a chuckle during his week off. “The money is one thing — it’s a little more on the PGA Tour — but knowing how I was playing, I thought I could move up in the fall standings.” Ben Kohles ‘betting on myself’ in pursuit of 2027 PGA Tour card Ben Kohles had one objective, and that was to lock up a PGA Tour card for 2027. He had two options and chose to follow his hunch. Associated Press , Associated Press , Walker, 31, is the youngest of the players currently in the tournament's top five after posting a bogey-free 30 on his first nine holes in Bermuda thanks to an eagle at the par-5 17th. He and Kohles are both University of Virginia alums. Byrd, a five-time PGA Tour winner, is the veteran of the group at 48 years old. He last won on the PGA Tour in the 2011 Hyundai Tournament of Champions. An eagle at the par-5 seventh hole propelled Byrd to a 6-under 30 on the front nine. He was bogey-free through 15 holes before missing a par putt at the same par 3 that tripped up Kohles. Hughes, 35, is looking to snap a four-year winless drought this week in Bermuda. He started at the 10th hole on Thursday, posting par across the first five holes. He was dominant the rest of the way, finding birdies at Nos. 15 and 17 before posting a 4-under 31 across the final nine holes — good for a bogey-free 64. item.title: What should the Oregon Ducks expect from Illinois' defense?
item.description: An afternoon trip to Champaign is on deck for the Oregon Ducks' stumbling offense, which might be just what the doctor ordered, facing an Illinois defense that has already made several sweeping changes during a trying season in the Midwest. Illinois made a coordinator change on defense a few weeks ago after a blowout loss to Ohio State, and things haven't been much better since. The Illini have wins over UAB and Southern Illinois, as well as an overtime victory over Michigan State heading into the bye week. However, in losses to Ohio State, Duke and Purdue, the Illini have allowed an average of 32.3 points. In an odd turn of events, the stoppable force that has been Oregon's offense the past two weeks will meet the movable object that is Illinois' defense, which could lead to a mundane collision or a breakthrough for one side. The Ducks will likely roll into the game without their starting quarterback Dante Moore , meaning it will once again come down to Dan Lanning to decide on the backup that will get under center. Despite some of the unit's struggles, Illinois does some interesting things defensively that could give the Ducks some trouble. Let's take a look at what Illinois does on defense schematically, who to look out for, and what the Ducks might be able to do to put points on the board. What does Illinois do well on defense? Illinois' defense hasn't been great this season, even since firing Bobby Hauck midseason and switching to Roger Cooper as the play-caller and defensive coordinator. The Illini run a 3-3-5 defense, stacking their defensive linemen and linebackers while primarily playing out of a nickel look in the secondary. Lanning noted this week how difficult the 3-3 stack can be to game plan for because of the varying pressures and rotations the defense can do in the secondary to change the picture for the quarterback. The Illini use a lot of twists and stunts up front while often blitzing a linebacker or defensive back to disguise the pressure. The defensive formation also allows for a late shift and pre-snap movement to counter offensive motion in an attempt to confuse the quarterback before the snap about what type of coverage they are facing. Despite the poor numbers the Illinois defense has put up this season, they have a lot of unique wrinkles that force an opposing offense to play fundamentally sound, rather than overly aggressive in any particular area. There is also plenty of athleticism and experience on this defense. More than half of the regular starters and rotational pieces are seniors with great speed and ability. There is no shortage of experience on the defensive side that can be difficult for a struggling offense to take on, especially on the road.
