item.content:encoded: An afternoon trip to Champaign is on deck for the Oregon Ducks' stumbling offense, which might be just what the doctor ordered, facing an Illinois defense that has already made several sweeping changes during a trying season in the Midwest. Illinois made a coordinator change on defense a few weeks ago after a blowout loss to Ohio State, and things haven't been much better since. The Illini have wins over UAB and Southern Illinois, as well as an overtime victory over Michigan State heading into the bye week. However, in losses to Ohio State, Duke and Purdue, the Illini have allowed an average of 32.3 points. In an odd turn of events, the stoppable force that has been Oregon's offense the past two weeks will meet the movable object that is Illinois' defense, which could lead to a mundane collision or a breakthrough for one side. The Ducks will likely roll into the game without their starting quarterback Dante Moore , meaning it will once again come down to Dan Lanning to decide on the backup that will get under center. Despite some of the unit's struggles, Illinois does some interesting things defensively that could give the Ducks some trouble. Let's take a look at what Illinois does on defense schematically, who to look out for, and what the Ducks might be able to do to put points on the board. What does Illinois do well on defense? Illinois' defense hasn't been great this season, even since firing Bobby Hauck midseason and switching to Roger Cooper as the play-caller and defensive coordinator. The Illini run a 3-3-5 defense, stacking their defensive linemen and linebackers while primarily playing out of a nickel look in the secondary. Lanning noted this week how difficult the 3-3 stack can be to game plan for because of the varying pressures and rotations the defense can do in the secondary to change the picture for the quarterback. The Illini use a lot of twists and stunts up front while often blitzing a linebacker or defensive back to disguise the pressure. The defensive formation also allows for a late shift and pre-snap movement to counter offensive motion in an attempt to confuse the quarterback before the snap about what type of coverage they are facing. Despite the poor numbers the Illinois defense has put up this season, they have a lot of unique wrinkles that force an opposing offense to play fundamentally sound, rather than overly aggressive in any particular area. There is also plenty of athleticism and experience on this defense. More than half of the regular starters and rotational pieces are seniors with great speed and ability. There is no shortage of experience on the defensive side that can be difficult for a struggling offense to take on, especially on the road. Both linebackers in the middle of the defense, Ismael Kante and James Kreutz, are seniors among the team leaders in tackles and lead the Illini in tackles for loss, figuring out ways to play behind the line of scrimmage and create negative plays. Players to know DE Will Holmes For a team that ranks dead last in the Big Ten with five sacks, Will Holmes is the primary pass rusher to keep an eye on. Holmes is often on the move and rarely rushes from an on-set position. He can float around the defense, twist and stunt at the snap, and he is one of the better pressure generators in the conference, tied with Oregon's Teitum Tuioti for seventh in the Big Ten with 19 pressures. He only has one sack this season, but Holmes is a solid player up front. S Matthew Bailey Matthew Bailey is a three-year starter for the Illini and a hulking defensive back in the secondary, standing at 6-foot-2 and 225 pounds. He leads the defense with 41 tackles and had a long pick-six earlier this season against Southern Illinois. Bailey led the Illini in tackles the past two seasons and is excellent at stepping up from his safety position and fitting against the run. As a last line of defense, Bailey is as sound a tackler as there is in the Big Ten. CB Juice Clarke Illinois' pass defense has been dreadful this season, and Juice Clarke has been beat at times this season. But Clarke is as feisty as they come, notably going toe-to-toe and jawing with Jeremiah Smith the past two seasons. He will be the Illini's top cover corner this weekend against Oregon's prolific receiving core, although the group is expected to be without key weapons in Jeremiah McClellan and Evan Stewart . Clarke has 26 tackles this season and leads the team with six deflections. Are the Ducks built to score on Illinois? Even the worst version of this Oregon offense should be able to score on this Illinois defense. The Illini have allowed 31.4 points and allow 248.3 passing yards per game this season, which ranks 114th in the nation. The Illini also allow 126.8 rushing yards per game, which ranks 49th in the country, so the Ducks could be able to build on some of the success they had in the fourth quarter last week against Nebraska, using the run game to ultimately come back and win the game. No matter who is under center for Oregon, whether it is Dylan Raiola or Brock Thomas making their second start of the season, there should be more opportunities downfield. Thomas is clearly limited in his ability to push the ball, but Raiola could force Illinois' defense to respect both facets of the offense on the ground and through the air. There are creative pressures that Cooper can disguise and scheme to throw at Oregon's quarterbacks and inexperienced offensive line, but even with some of that creativity, the Illini defensive line has not found much success this season, managing just five sacks to this point. Illinois also only has three takeaways this season, so there is less of a threat when it comes to Raiola's decision-making and occasional carelessness with the ball in his hands. This is a game where Oregon's offense can absolutely get right and put up a bunch of points, so long as the Ducks play sound and don't try to force the action and let the home crowd make an impact on the game. What should we expect? I expect the Illini to stick to the 3-3 stack and try to find ways to get after the quarterback. Illinois could be extra aggressive up front to help support their own backup quarterback, Michael Clayton II, much like Oregon's defense has improved its play since Moore has been sidelined. That could be a point of emphasis after the Illini had the bye week to prepare for the Ducks, hoping to create more turnovers and short fields for the offense. I think Oregon will try to take advantage of Illinois' deficiencies against the pass, but the battle on the ground will be one to watch. The Ducks' offensive line appeared to take a step forward in the second half against Nebraska, but Illinois has great tacklers and experienced eyes in the second and third levels of the defense that are great fits against the run, so it could develop into a very physical battle on the ground. Oregon has the assets to score quickly and often against Illinois, even with just decent quarterback play, so it will come down to whether the Illini are able to force turnovers and make the Ducks beat themselves. Oregon will also be relying on freshmen receivers like Messiah Hampton , Jalen Lott and Gatlin Bair , so the Ducks will need to spread the defense out and make the simple plays to win. The Ducks don't have to score fast; they just need to find ways to score touchdowns instead of field goals, which has been a struggle lately. Contact/Follow @Ducks_Wire on X (formerly Twitter) and like our page on Facebook to follow ongoing coverage of Oregon Ducks news, notes, and opinion s. item.title: Briarcrest adds to TSSAA volleyball dynasty with another DII-AA state championship
item.description: MURFREESBORO — The word "dynasty" doesn't intimidate the Briarcrest volleyball team. After winning their second consecutive TSSAA volleyball state championship in Division II-AA, and fifth in seven years, are the Saints building a dynasty? "I think we have one already," said Briarcrest coach April Jaurequi, following her squad's 3-2 win over CPA in the title match on Oct. 22 at MTSU's Murphy Center. "So, the hard part is sustaining it. But we're incredibly fortunate with the athletes we have at our school, and Briarcrest does a great job supporting us." SOCCER: TSSAA girls soccer region tournament brackets, schedules, scores for Memphis area Briarcrest has been to the DII-AA state championship match 11 of the past 12 years, winning the title seven times during that stretch. This wasn't the easiest of the titles for the Saints (32-7). Briarcrest lost in the opening round to Father Ryan before digging its way out of the losers bracket to reach the finals. And for the second straight season, CPA (29-6) took the Saints to five sets, 25-15, 17-25, 25-19, 15-25, 15-9. "If you're a good team, you know how to come back stronger every time, every set," said Briacrest junior outside hitter Ashari Jenkins, who was named state finals MVP with 28 kills and 17 digs. "I thought we did a better job in the fifth set, coming out and making sure that we're on top." The match flip-flopped, with the two teams trading sets until the fifth. The Lions and Saints were tied at 8 in the fifth until back-to-back Jenkins kills gave Briarcrest a lead it wouldn't relinquish. Camille Northcross had 11 kills and Allison Floyd had 52 assists for Briarcrest. CPA was led by freshman Sophia Freije with 19 kills while junior Taylor Willeford added 18. The Lions, who have reached the state title match two consecutive seasons (also taking Briarcrest to five sets in 2025), are hoping they are building something special as well. "The last two years have been great," said CPA coach Carrol Denure, about a CPA program that had reached state only twice prior to 2025. "We've been building the culture and the program, from our middle school all the way up. I don't think we're a one-and-done program at all." Cecil Joyce covers high school sports and MTSU athletics for The Daily News Journal. Contact him at cjoyce@dnj.com and follow him on X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, @Cecil_Joyce. "If you're a good team, you know how to come back stronger every time, every set," said Briacrest junior outside hitter Ashari Jenkins, who was named state finals MVP with 28 kills and 17 digs. "I thought we did a better job in the fifth set, coming out and making sure that we're on top." The match flip-flopped, with the two teams trading sets until the fifth. The Lions and Saints were tied at 8 in the fifth until back-to-back Jenkins kills gave Briarcrest a lead it wouldn't relinquish. Camille Northcross had 11 kills and Allison Floyd had 52 assists for Briarcrest. CPA was led by freshman Sophia Freije with 19 kills while junior Taylor Willeford added 18. The Lions, who have reached the state title match two consecutive seasons (also taking Briarcrest to five sets in 2025), are hoping they are building something special as well. "The last two years have been great," said CPA coach Carrol Denure, about a CPA program that had reached state only twice prior to 2025. "We've been building the culture and the program, from our middle school all the way up. I don't think we're a one-and-done program at all." Cecil Joyce covers high school sports and MTSU athletics for The Daily News Journal. Contact him at cjoyce@dnj.com and follow him on X, the platform formerly known as Twitter, @Cecil_Joyce. item.title: Vance tells Republicans to 'stop whining' after Ramaswamy attack ad in Ohio governor's race
item.description: US Vice President JD Vance on Wednesday defended an explosive attack ad by Republican Vivek Ramaswamy’s campaign against his Democratic rival in the Ohio governor’s race, telling fellow Republicans to "stop whining" about it and go win the race. The ad features ​Democrat Amy Acton’s ‌estranged mother, Donna Arthur, disputing Acton’s account of a childhood she says involved a period of homelessness and sexual abuse. ⁠Arthur, whom Acton says she has not seen since 1978, urges Ohioans not to vote for her daughter. Acton has said she was sexually abused by her stepfather when she was 12. Her mother stayed with the ‌stepfather, who was charged with rape but fled the state and was never tried. He died in 2004. Acton said she ⁠and her brother were removed from her mother's custody for severe abuse, neglect and sexual abuse. Acton's brother has supported her account. FRANCE 24's Catherine Viette reports.

item.title: "Disillusioned" MAHA leader quits as Trump admin's food agenda spoils: Report
item.description: Calley Means—a top ally to anti-vaccine Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and a co-author of the so-called "MAHA bible"—resigned from his role in the Trump administration Thursday, reportedly in frustration over delays to food policy changes sought by the Make America Healthy Again movement. "I am resigning from the White House with tremendous respect for President Trump and Bobby Kennedy," Means wrote in a social media post this afternoon . "It was an honor to advocate for MAHA moms in the administration and steer policies like Dietary Guidelines reform, psychedelic reform, removing soda from SNAP, removing food dyes, GRAS reform, and overhauling government food procurement." His post did not provide a reason for his departure. Means served as a senior advisor to Kennedy. Read full article Comments

item.title: Makurdi in darkness as electricity workers withdraw services over alleged attack
item.description: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State capital, Makurdi, has been thrown into darkness following the withdrawal of services by members of the National Union of Electricity Employees, NUEE, in the Jos Electricity Distribution Plc, JED, chapter, over an alleged attack on some of its members by suspected armed men. The union alleged that the attackers invaded the Makurdi District office of JED, seized the Benue State Operating Officer, Mr. Samson Abah, and an unspecified number of other workers before taking them to the River Benue Bridge, where they were reportedly assaulted. According to the union, the attackers also seized the workers’ mobile phones and other personal belongings, demanded money for their release and allegedly forced them to reconnect electricity supply to the Benue State Government House. The Acting National Secretary of NUEE, Dominic Igwebike, who disclosed this in a statement, said the incident followed the disconnection of electricity supply to Government House over an alleged discovery of meter bypass by government officials. The union’s position came amid an escalating disagreement over electricity supply to the state government’s seat of power, with the Benue State Government dismissing the allegations and accusing JED of making unsubstantiated claims against it. Igwebike said the union could no longer guarantee the safety of its members if they continued to work under the prevailing circumstances, insisting that the withdrawal of services was necessary to protect their lives and property. He said, “Our members cannot continue to work under their brutalised, intimidation and threats to life until we are assured of the safety of our lives and properties.” Confirming the shutdown of electricity supply to Makurdi, a JED staff member, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak on the matter, said the workers withdrew their services following the alleged attack on their colleagues. “Our office was attacked and our union asked us to withdraw our services, so we have shut down power supply to Makurdi. We have left the office after shutting down, and Makurdi will not have power supply until the matter is resolved with our union,” the staff member said. However, the Benue State Government has strongly rejected the allegations, describing them as baseless, defamatory and an attempt to tarnish its image. item.dc:creator: Henry Oduah
item.content:encoded: By Peter Duru, Makurdi The Benue State capital, Makurdi, has been thrown into darkness following the withdrawal of services by members of the National Union of Electricity Employees, NUEE, in the Jos Electricity Distribution Plc, JED, chapter, over an alleged attack on some of its members by suspected armed men. The union alleged that the attackers invaded the Makurdi District office of JED, seized the Benue State Operating Officer, Mr. Samson Abah, and an unspecified number of other workers before taking them to the River Benue Bridge, where they were reportedly assaulted. According to the union, the attackers also seized the workers’ mobile phones and other personal belongings, demanded money for their release and allegedly forced them to reconnect electricity supply to the Benue State Government House. The Acting National Secretary of NUEE, Dominic Igwebike, who disclosed this in a statement, said the incident followed the disconnection of electricity supply to Government House over an alleged discovery of meter bypass by government officials. The union’s position came amid an escalating disagreement over electricity supply to the state government’s seat of power, with the Benue State Government dismissing the allegations and accusing JED of making unsubstantiated claims against it. Igwebike said the union could no longer guarantee the safety of its members if they continued to work under the prevailing circumstances, insisting that the withdrawal of services was necessary to protect their lives and property. He said, “Our members cannot continue to work under their brutalised, intimidation and threats to life until we are assured of the safety of our lives and properties.” Confirming the shutdown of electricity supply to Makurdi, a JED staff member, who spoke on condition of anonymity because he was not authorised to speak on the matter, said the workers withdrew their services following the alleged attack on their colleagues. “Our office was attacked and our union asked us to withdraw our services, so we have shut down power supply to Makurdi. We have left the office after shutting down, and Makurdi will not have power supply until the matter is resolved with our union,” the staff member said. However, the Benue State Government has strongly rejected the allegations, describing them as baseless, defamatory and an attempt to tarnish its image. In a statement issued by the Commissioner for Information, Chief Solomon Iorpev, the government said it would not accept allegations linking it to violence, abduction or illegal electricity connections without credible evidence. The statement read, “The Government of Benue State strongly rejects the baseless and defamatory allegations contained in the press statement issued by Jos Electricity Distribution Plc (JED Plc) on October 22, 2026. The claims that the State Government sanctioned acts of violence, abduction, or illegal electricity connections are reckless, unfounded, and unacceptable.” Addressing the allegations surrounding the reported attack on JED workers, the government questioned the evidence linking it to the incident, arguing that the distribution company had not provided verifiable details to substantiate its claims. According to the statement: “JED Plc’s own use of the word ‘allegedly’ confirms that it has no evidence linking the Government to the incident of October 21, 2026. No names, identities, or credible references were provided. The Government categorically rejects this insinuation.” On the dispute over electricity supply to Government House, the state government said issues concerning transformer energisation and alleged metering irregularities should be handled through the appropriate regulatory and judicial channels. It stated, “Issues of transformer energization and metering irregularities are regulatory matters. They must be addressed before the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) and, where necessary, the courts, not through inflammatory press releases. “Assertions of abduction, assault, and injuries remain unsubstantiated. The Government does not condone violence and demands that impartial, evidence-based, and transparent investigations be carried out by security operatives,” the statement added. Expressing displeasure over JED’s handling of the controversy, the government described the company’s public reaction as premature, arguing that it should have allowed security agencies to establish the facts before making allegations in the media. “The reckless outburst by the JED without conclusive investigations is suspicious and amounts to sponsorship by enemies of state to tarnish the image of the government,” the statement alleged. The government also faulted JED’s reference to an earlier incident on September 3, 2026, describing the company’s account as misleading. It challenged the distribution company to produce documentary evidence of its alleged previous communications with the state government over the dispute. “The company has failed to produce records of its alleged ‘several communications’ with the Government. The State challenges JED Plc to publish such correspondence if it exists,” the statement said. Insisting that electricity distribution companies must comply with the same regulatory requirements and safety standards applicable to their customers, the government said JED must also be held accountable for its operations. The statement added: “JED Plc itself acknowledges that interventions must comply with regulatory requirements and safety standards. The Government insists that this standard binds JED Plc as firmly as it binds any customer, including public institutions.” The state government further warned JED against what it described as attempts to politicise its operations and damage the integrity of the state. “The Benue State Government will not tolerate attempts by any business entity to politicize its operations or malign the integrity of the State. JED Plc is hereby strongly warned to desist from making baseless accusations in the media,” it said. Consequently, the government demanded the immediate withdrawal of what it described as the insinuation that it sanctioned violence, a retraction of the allegation that it engaged in meter bypassing or illegal electricity connections, and a formal apology to the government and the people of Benue State. It warned that it would consider legal action if JED persisted in disseminating what it described as false information. “The Government remains committed to the rule of law, the protection of lives and property, and constructive engagement with stakeholders in the electricity sector. However, it will not hesitate to pursue legal remedies should JED Plc persist in disseminating falsehoods,” the statement said. The government added that the people of Benue State deserved reliable electricity supply, respectful treatment and accountability rather than what it termed reckless allegations. As of the time of filing this report, the dispute had resulted in a shutdown of electricity supply to Makurdi, with the workers insisting that they would not resume operations until the matter was resolved with their union. The post Makurdi in darkness as electricity workers withdraw services over alleged attack appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: S’East assemblies back state police, warn against political abuse
item.description: By Steve Oko, Vin Ujumadu, Chinedu Adonu & Jeff Agbodo The various Houses of Assembly in the South-East have backed the Bill for State Police. While Anambra , Enugu, Imo and Abia have passed the Bill, Ebonyi House of Assembly is at the verge of passing it into law. The executive bill, which originated from the Presidency, was passed through the first, second and third readings during plenary on Tuesday. The proposed framework allows states to establish their own police services, subject to constitutional provisions and national policing standards prescribed by the National Assembly. Presiding over the plenary, Speaker, Anambra State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Somtochukwu Udeze, directed the Clerk to transmit the resolution to the National Assembly. The Majority Leader, Ikenna Ofodeme, said state police would strengthen grassroots security, facilitate quicker responses to threats, create jobs and reduce the military’s involvement in internal security operations. He also proposed integrating local vigilantes into the state policing system after appropriate training. Throwing their weight behind the Bill, the Enugu State House of Assembly, said decentralising the country’s policing architecture would improve security and strengthen the protection of lives and property. The lawmakers expressed their positions on Tuesday, November 20 during plenary while considering a proposed constitutional amendment to provide for the establishment of State Police Service and related matters. Supporting the proposal, the member representing Ezeagu Constituency, Hon. Chima Obieze, said the establishment of state police would make policing more effective by bringing security operations closer to the people. According to him: “The establishment of State Police will decentralise the policing architecture of the country and make it more effective in the protection of lives and property across the state.” Similarly, the member representing Nkanu East Constituency, Hon. Okey Mbah, said state police could help tackle recurring security challenges, including violence and attacks attributed to herders in different parts of the state. Mbah maintained that a decentralised policing system would enable authorities to respond more effectively to security threats within their respective communities. He said the establishment of state police would help “curtail incessant violence and herdsmen attacks in different parts of the state.” However, the member representing Igbo-Eze South Constituency, Hon. Harrison Ogara, cautioned that the proposed state police system could be abused by political officeholders if adequate safeguards were not established. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Steve Oko, Vin Ujumadu, Chinedu Adonu & Jeff Agbodo The various Houses of Assembly in the South-East have backed the Bill for State Police. While Anambra , Enugu, Imo and Abia have passed the Bill, Ebonyi House of Assembly is at the verge of passing it into law. The executive bill, which originated from the Presidency, was passed through the first, second and third readings during plenary on Tuesday. The proposed framework allows states to establish their own police services, subject to constitutional provisions and national policing standards prescribed by the National Assembly. Presiding over the plenary, Speaker, Anambra State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Somtochukwu Udeze, directed the Clerk to transmit the resolution to the National Assembly. The Majority Leader, Ikenna Ofodeme, said state police would strengthen grassroots security, facilitate quicker responses to threats, create jobs and reduce the military’s involvement in internal security operations. He also proposed integrating local vigilantes into the state policing system after appropriate training. Throwing their weight behind the Bill, the Enugu State House of Assembly, said decentralising the country’s policing architecture would improve security and strengthen the protection of lives and property. The lawmakers expressed their positions on Tuesday, November 20 during plenary while considering a proposed constitutional amendment to provide for the establishment of State Police Service and related matters. Supporting the proposal, the member representing Ezeagu Constituency, Hon. Chima Obieze, said the establishment of state police would make policing more effective by bringing security operations closer to the people. According to him: “The establishment of State Police will decentralise the policing architecture of the country and make it more effective in the protection of lives and property across the state.” Similarly, the member representing Nkanu East Constituency, Hon. Okey Mbah, said state police could help tackle recurring security challenges, including violence and attacks attributed to herders in different parts of the state. Mbah maintained that a decentralised policing system would enable authorities to respond more effectively to security threats within their respective communities. He said the establishment of state police would help “curtail incessant violence and herdsmen attacks in different parts of the state.” However, the member representing Igbo-Eze South Constituency, Hon. Harrison Ogara, cautioned that the proposed state police system could be abused by political officeholders if adequate safeguards were not established. Ogara expressed concern that state police formations might be used to intimidate political opponents, stressing that effective oversight and accountability mechanisms were necessary to protect the institution from political interference. He said: “State Police formations could be used to intimidate political opponents if adequate safeguards are not put in place.” The lawmaker also called for professional standards, transparent accountability structures and sustainable funding arrangements to ensure that state police personnel discharge their duties without undue political influence. According to him, effective oversight would be essential to ensuring that the proposed security structure serves the public interest rather than the interests of those in power. The Speaker of the House, Chief Uche Ugwu, said the proposed changes to the naming of Nigeria’s policing institutions could also influence institutional orientation and the attitudes of personnel. The proposal includes changing the name of the Nigeria Police Force to the Federal Police Service, alongside the establishment of the State Police Service. Ugwu said the changes could contribute to a shift in institutional orientation and personnel attitudes, potentially improving the delivery of policing services. The proposed constitutional amendment comes amid growing calls for the decentralisation of Nigeria’s security architecture to enable states to respond more effectively to local security challenges. Proponents argue that state police would improve intelligence gathering and response times, while critics have raised concerns about possible political abuse, inadequate funding and the need for strong accountability mechanisms. Ebonyi to pass bill soon — Speaker The Speaker of the Ebonyi State House of Assembly, Rt. Hon. Moses Ije Odunwa, has said the Assembly will soon pass the State Police Bill. Odunwa disclosed that lawmakers had commenced deliberations on the bill and were close to completing the process, subject to necessary scrutiny. He said the proposed legislation was aimed at strengthening the protection of lives and property in Ebonyi State and Nigeria at large. The Speaker recalled that Ebonyi State had supported the establishment of state police during the National Assembly’s constitutional review engagement, where the state government and Assembly made submissions in favour of decentralised policing. “We have started deliberating on the bill, and we are very close to its passage,” Odunwa said. Similarly, the Deputy Speaker, Abia State House of Assembly, Austin Nmeregini, told Vanguard on Thursday afternoon that the Abia lawmakers were at the verge of passing the Bill. He disclosed that the Bill had already received the support of the lawmakers during their Executive session, hinting that they were proceeding into plenary where it will ultimately be passed into law. He said that the passage of the Bill into law would help address peculiar security challenges of every state as every state better understands its own terrain more than strangers. Later in the day, the Abia State House of Assembly voted in favour of the State Police Bill. The Acting Clerk Abia State House of Assembly, Mr Promise confirmed this in an interview with Vanguard. Speaking later with Vanguard, Deputy Speaker Nmeregini, said that the State Police Bill was passed by “unanimous vote.” The post S’East assemblies back state police, warn against political abuse appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Electric or gas? BMW goes both ways with new 2027 X5 and iX5.
item.description: BMW provided flights from Washington, DC, to Los Angeles and accommodation so Ars could drive the new X5 and iX5, as well as a refreshed i7 (which you can read about soon). Ars does not accept paid editorial content. When we first drove BMW’s first Neue Klasse model, the iX3 , it quickly revealed that BMW knows how to make a good electric vehicle. A clean-sheet design, it featured the automaker’s sixth-generation electric powertrain , a completely reimagined dashboard, and powerful computers to run the whole show. Now, much of that technology is being ported over to the larger X5 line. But BMW knows not all its customers are ready to go electric, especially in the US, so it’s sticking with its powertrain-agnostic CLAR platform, as used in cars as diverse as the large 7 Series and the new gasoline 3 Series. Which means in addition to the all-electric iX5, there are also mild hybrid and plug-in hybrid X5s available, and in time, even a hydrogen-powered option. For now, as I’ll explain, I think the EV is the pick of the bunch. Get used to it, because this is what BMW SUV kidney grilles look like from now on. Credit: BMW If you looked very carefully you'd see this was an iX5 because there's no exhausts. Of course, reading the badge is probably easier. Credit: BMW Pick your power The most conventional option is the X5 40 xDrive, powered by a 3.0 L turbocharged inline six-cylinder engine that generates 394 hp (294 kW) and 428 lb-ft (580 Nm). The 48 V mild hybrid system can contribute a decent slug of torque (148 lb-ft/200 Nm) if necessary, and the engine operates under the Miller cycle for better efficiency, as well as featuring the usual BMW engine technology, like variable valve timing. Expect around 26 mpg (9 L/100 km) from this powertrain and a full-to-empty range of 569 miles (915 km). Read full article Comments

The 48 V mild hybrid system can contribute a decent slug of torque (148 lb-ft/200 Nm) if necessary, and the engine operates under the Miller cycle for better efficiency, as well as featuring the usual BMW engine technology, like variable valve timing. Expect around 26 mpg (9 L/100 km) from this powertrain and a full-to-empty range of 569 miles (915 km). Read full article Comments

item.title: Discord now formats Markdown previews right
item.description: Discord's latest update released today has a big improvement for Markdown previews: they should now render correctly instead of with "a bunch of symbols," according to the company. LLMs and AI agents often rely on Markdown files for instructions and context, so these improved previews could be helpful for people sharing information about AI projects on the platform. item.title: Domestic crude supply to refineries falls 6.3% — NMDPRA
item.description: — Petrol supply drops 20.6% By Obas Esiedesa, Abuja Domestic crude oil supply to Nigerian refineries fell by 6.3 per cent to 15.97 million barrels in September 2026 from 17.05 million barrels in August, while petrol supply from domestic refineries also declined amid reduced imports. The September 2026 Midstream and Downstream Report released by the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA) on Thursday showed that average daily petrol receipts dropped by 23.4 per cent to 38.7 million litres from 50.5 million litres in August. The report attributed the decline to lower domestic supply and reduced imports following the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes. Between January and September 2026, Nigerian refineries received a combined 156.51 million barrels of crude oil, comprising 125.85 million barrels of domestic crude and 30.66 million barrels of imported crude. Domestic crude accounted for 80.4 per cent of total refinery intake during the period, while imported crude contributed 19.6 per cent. The report also showed that Dangote Refinery operated at 105.98 per cent utilisation in September, processing approximately 689,000 barrels of crude oil per day against average crude receipts of 618,000 barrels per day. The difference of about 71,000 barrels per day was drawn from the refinery’s inventory, indicating that it processed more crude than it received during the month. On petrol supply, the NMDPRA data showed that domestic refineries supplied an average of 28.5 million litres per day in September, down 20.6 per cent from 35.9 million litres in August. Petrol imports also declined by 30.1 per cent to 10.2 million litres per day from 14.6 million litres. Despite the decline, domestic refineries remained the largest source of petrol supply, accounting for approximately 73.6 per cent of total receipts in September, compared with 26.4 per cent from imports. The September average of 38.7 million litres per day was also below the 13-month average of 49.7 million litres per day recorded between September 2025 and September 2026. Over the 13-month period, domestic refineries supplied an average of 30.4 million litres of petrol per day, representing 61.2 per cent of total supply, while imports contributed 19.3 million litres per day, or 38.8 per cent. The NMDPRA reiterated that September’s decline in petrol receipts reflected a 21 per cent drop in domestic supply from August levels and a 30 per cent reduction in imports amid the exhaustion of approved import permit volumes. The post Domestic crude supply to refineries falls 6.3% — NMDPRA appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Targeted by Trump, International Criminal Court wins top EU rights prize
item.description: Facing US sanctions, the International Criminal Court was on Thursday awarded the European Union's top rights prize, in a show of support that risks upsetting President Donald Trump. "The European Union is built on respect for multilateralism and international institutions, and this prize recognises the important work of the court in upholding international law and justice," said European Parliament chief Roberta Metsola in announcing the award. The ICC thanked the European Parliament for giving it the Sakharov Prize "at a time when the Court and its officials face unprecedented challenges". FRANCE 24's International Affairs Commentator Douglas Herbert has more.

item.title: Edo govt demolishes building allegedly used for organ harvesting, cultism
item.description: By Ozioruva Aliu A house in Uwalor-Oke in Uromi, Esan North East Local Government Area of Edo State has been demolished for allegedly being used for cult activities and organ harvesting. Besides the demolition, the suspected organ harvester Ebhata Eromosele was also arrested by the Edo State Special Security Squad codenamed Operation Flush out Kidnapping and Cultists, in collaboration with Edo State Security Corps, the Nigerian Police Force and other sister security agencies, supervised by the Principal Security Officer (PSO) to the governor. The building was said to have been used for ritual activities where Eromosele was alleged to have harvested the organs of three young women, out of which one of the victims, a pregnant woman, died in the process; one who was hospitalised has been discharged while another is receiving treatment in an undisclosed hospital in Esan Central Senatorial District. Another building located at Idi-Negbon Eguare Ewatto, allegedly used for cult-related activities, was also not spared as it was touched by bulldozers. In a statement by Governor Monday Okpebholo’s Chief Press Secretary, Dr. Patrick Ebiojele, the coordinator of the Special Security Squad, Amiolemen Idemudia said criminals would be wiped out of Edo State. He noted that Ebhata Eromosele engaged in ritual activities before nemesis caught up with him and have been arrested and today his building is demolished in Uromi. He said, “A lifeless body killed and dumped was traced by Edo State Security Corps to this bungalow apartment used by the suspect. “A search of this residence exposed the suspect as security operative saw bloodstained bedspread and other incriminating evidence indicating that Ebhata is into ritual activities and organ harvesting.” Idemudia said the governor has warned that his administration will not tolerate crime of this nature and will make the state unsafe for criminal elements. On the cult issue, Idemudia said there were cult fracas in Ewatto disturbing the peace of the community. He said that one Bright Ejetuwamen was at the forefront of the fight, using his properties at Ewatto for cult-related activities. He said the property has been demolished. “Governor Monday Okpebholo will not spare any hideout or properties used to perpetrate crime as it will be demolished. The cultist has been apprehended. All criminals must leave Edo State,” he said. The Zonal Commander, Edo State Security Corps, SP Johnson Oyameda (rtd), said the success recorded in the arrest of the ritual suspect was as a result of over a month of surveillance. “The body of a lady mutilated and dumped in a drainage was recovered while still alive. Not up to two weeks another body was recovered again and these incidents led to stepping up surveillance around the area and the surveillance paid off. “Ebhata Eromosele murdered a lady and dumped the body but my men on surveillance saw him and trailed him to this apartment which has been demolished today,” he said. Both the suspected

item.title: Lego Confirms Incredible Daft Punk Set for Official Release
item.description: Lego is officially teaming up with Daft Punk for new "products, content and brand experiences," the toymaker announced Thursday. But that's apparently just the start of what the brands have in store.

item.title: Samsung all but confirms iPhone Duo is goosing Galaxy Z8 sales
item.description: Android-powered foldable phones have been available for years, but most people never paid attention to them. As predicted, that could be changing now that Apple has entered the folding phone market with the iPhone Duo . Analysts have speculated that Samsung's Z8 foldables were seeing a boost from the iPhone announcement, and now Samsung has seemingly confirmed that. In a new blog post , Samsung UK crows that the company's 2026 foldable lineup is moving much faster than last year's models. Compared to the Galaxy Z Fold 7, combined European sales for the Galaxy Z Fold 8 and Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra are up 45 percent. Samsung isn't talking about Z Flip 8 sales, but it previously noted that its larger foldables made up about 80 percent of foldable purchases. We can assume any increase there is not impressive enough to mention. The reason for flat Z Flip sales may simply be that Apple didn't release a flip phone. Unsurprisingly, Samsung doesn't mention Apple or the iPhone Duo in its press release. However, it does say that search volume for the Z8 series across Europe spiked 460 percent the week of September 6 to 12. And guess what was announced on September 9? Yep, the iPhone Duo. Z Fold 8 search volume across the entire month of September (when the phones launched) was up 260 percent. Read full article Comments

item.title: The new Fire TV Stick 4K is already half off
item.description: Despite being announced just a few weeks ago , both Amazon and Best Buy are now offering the latest Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K for 50 percent off, bringing the price down to an all-time low of $29.99. The most notable new feature is that the Fire TV Stick 4K no longer requires a separate power connection, meaning it can draw all the juice it needs from the USB port on your TV. It supports 4K at up to 60fps, with HDR10 Plus for higher contrast, although it’s worth noting that it doesn’t allow for side-loading apps like some older models. Amazon Fire TV Stick 4K (2026) Where to Buy: $59.99 $29.99 at Amazon $59.99 $29.99 at Best Buy Amazon updated the Fire TV OS earlier this year with a redesigned UI, closer Alexa Plus integration, and various improvements to the mobile app, all of which are supported on the new hardware. You’ll also get a revamped remote, which features a new asymmetrical design with a rounded bottom and buttons with a more tactile feel. For connectivity, the Fire TV Stick 4K has Bluetooth 5.3 and Wi-Fi 6.

item.title: Refurbished PS5 consoles include second controller for an extra $18
item.description: A lot of people are snagging a PlayStation 5 ahead of Grand Theft Auto VI ’s November 19th launch. You could pay full price at one of many retailers, but why do that when you can save $100 on a Sony-refurbished console that has the same one-year warranty? It’s a great time to consider one because company has a new limited-time bundle. Through this page , you can select either a refurbished digital or disc-based console for $499 or $549, respectively, and add a refurbished DualSense to your order that’s $40 off its usual price. For instance, a white DualSense tacks just $18 to your total, while one of the fancier colors, like sterling silver, adds $23. It’s an affordable way to stock up to cover a two-player household. The refurbished controller also includes a one-year warranty. Sony PlayStation 5 slim (refurbished) Where to Buy: $558 $518 at Sony (digital, with refurb DualSense) $608 $568 at Sony (disc, with refurb DualSense) One thing to note about the refurbished consoles is that they include a 1TB SSD. Sony’s digital edition console at stores is currently equipped with 825GB of built-in storage (the disc edition still has 1TB), so it’s nice that this version includes a little extra space for games. Like all PlayStation 5 consoles, these support PCIe 4.0 M.2 SSDs equipped with heatsinks for extra storage, though like RAM, those are pretty pricey at the moment.

item.title: Spain refers LaLiga chief to tribunal over Real Madrid Nazi comments
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye LaLiga president Javier Tebas has been referred to Spain’s sports tribunal over his comparison of Real Madrid’s communication tactics to Nazi propaganda, following the Spanish club’s demand for his resignation. According to Reuters, Spain’s National Sports Council (CSD) announced on Thursday that it had referred Tebas to the Administrative Court for Sport (TAD) to determine whether his remarks breached regulations protecting sporting dignity and decorum. The referral concerns comments Tebas made on social media on October 16, criticising Real Madrid’s handling of complaints about refereeing decisions and the club’s television coverage of match officials. Tebas accused Real Madrid of using communication tactics that recalled propaganda methods employed by Joseph Goebbels, Nazi Germany’s propaganda minister. Real Madrid subsequently demanded the immediate resignation of the 64-year-old, describing his comparison as unacceptable for someone holding the position of LaLiga president. However, Tebas insisted that he was referring to propaganda techniques rather than Nazi ideology or Real Madrid’s supporters. In its referral, the CSD asked the tribunal to assess whether the remarks could constitute a serious offence under Article 76.4.b of Spain’s 1990 Sports Law, which covers public acts that infringe upon sporting dignity or decorum. Possible sanctions for such offences include warnings, fines or suspension. The controversy followed Tebas’s criticism of Real Madrid’s efforts to challenge the standard of refereeing in Spanish football. The club has repeatedly questioned officiating decisions through its in-house television channel. In a fresh post on X on Thursday, Tebas defended his comments and questioned why Real Madrid’s accusations against Spanish referees had not attracted similar scrutiny under the rules governing sporting dignity. “Defending the competition also requires responding to those who constantly discredit it,” Tebas wrote, adding that he intended to continue exercising that responsibility. He also argued that Real Madrid’s repeated questioning of the integrity of Spanish football could itself be examined under the same rules. The AFP also reports that the CSD emphasised the importance of protecting respect, coexistence and fair play in sport. The tribunal will determine whether the matter warrants disciplinary proceedings. No finding of wrongdoing against Tebas has been announced. The post Spain refers LaLiga chief to tribunal over Real Madrid Nazi comments appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Delta can turn the iPhone Duo into your favorite folding handheld
item.description: The Duo has a Nintendo DS-like shape anyway, so Delta 2.0 is running with it. | Image: Riley Testut The Delta gaming emulator has been upgraded with a plethora of new goodies and support updates, which includes optimizing it for Apple's iPhone Duo. Delta 2.0 also introduces Sega Genesis games, animated controller skins, custom Pokémon DLC experiences, and a new UI that was built around supporting Liquid Glass. item.title: US official: Russia's stalker satellite sure looks like an orbital weapon
item.description: Four years ago, a senior official in Russia's foreign ministry painted a bullseye on commercial satellite networks that assist Ukraine in its fight against invading Russian military forces. On Wednesday, several days after a Russian military spacecraft moved within striking distance of one of those commercial satellites, the same Russian diplomat assured the world there's no reason to worry. There's a sharp incongruity in those statements from Konstantin Vorontsov, deputy head of Russia's delegation to the United Nations. Vorontsov's comments Wednesday in the UN General Assembly's First Committee came moments after a US official called attention to recent maneuvers by Kosmos 2612 , a Russian military craft that approached a US-registered commercial satellite some 340 miles (550 kilometers) above Earth. Read full article Comments

item.title: DSS arrests 23-year-old female arms courier in Nasarawa
item.description: — Sule commends security agencies over crackdown on arms trafficking By Edwin Philip LAFIA — Nasarawa State Governor, Abdullahi Sule, has commended the Department of State Services (DSS) for its sustained efforts to clamp down on gun runners and arms traffickers in the state following the arrest of a 23-year-old female suspected arms courier in Keffi. The governor’s commendation was contained in a statement issued on Thursday by his Press Secretary, Ibrahim Addra, who described the arrest of Aisha Mohammed, a resident of Bwari, Federal Capital Territory, as a significant breakthrough. According to the statement, Mohammed was arrested with 202 rounds of 7.62mm-calibre ammunition and three empty magazines. “The suspect, currently in custody, was arrested while in possession of 202 rounds of 7.62mm-calibre ammunition with three empty magazines,” the statement said. It added that other suspected arms couriers arrested between August and September 2026 included Hassan Sani, 40; Abdulkadir Idrissa, 41; and Salihu Garba, 70, also known as Nabayi. The statement said security operatives recovered 678 rounds of 7.62mm ammunition, 99 rounds of 7.5mm ammunition and other items from the suspects. It further disclosed that an alleged arms courier, Ismail Lawalli, a native of Zamfara State, was arrested in August along the Keffi-Abuja highway with 1,262 assorted rounds of ammunition. Sule praised DSS personnel and other security agencies in Nasarawa for their dedication and commitment to tackling arms trafficking and other criminal activities. He also commended the collaboration between the security agencies and his administration, pledging continued government support for their operations. The governor assured residents of his administration’s resolve to combat criminality and called on the public to support security agencies in maintaining peace and safety across the state. The post DSS arrests 23-year-old female arms courier in Nasarawa appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: In Meta’s version of the future, I’ll have my Muse call your Muse
item.description: Mark Zuckerberg is barrelling toward a future in which an autonomous network of AI agents will run our lives - shopping for us, working for us, talking to other people's AI agents for us. Are humans ready for this very specific and unrelenting vision of a life in which we communicate primarily through bot proxies? Actually, don't answer that. The more urgent question coming off Meta's quarterly earnings call Wednesday night is more likely to be: "Is he?" Zuckerberg is staking Meta's future on Muse, the personal AI agent it released to the general public last month. It's early days, but Zuckerberg told investors on Wednesday's call that he s … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Mass Effect 5 trailer leaks following BioWare shutdown
item.description: Yesterday, EA shut down BioWare and canceled the studio's new Mass Effect game in development, but a trailer apparently representing the game was published on Reddit today . The trailer features "in-engine footage" and uses "pre-production assets," according to a message at the beginning of the video. The video focuses on an ex-soldier in a conversation with a mysterious Asari character that sidles up to him at a bar, including a flashback to a fight that looks like modern-day version of the gameplay from the original trilogy. It all feels very Mass Effect , with humans and aliens species mingling together, cuts to brief action sequences, and … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: NAFDAC uncovers another fake herbal factory in Lagos, arrests manager
item.description: By Chioma obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) on Thursday uncovered another illegal herbal products factory in Agege, Lagos, where three unregistered products were allegedly manufactured under unhygienic conditions, with one bearing a registration number belonging to a registered cough syrup. The agency sealed the facility, evacuated the products and arrested the manager, identified as Abulaziz Sayidu, for interrogation, while the alleged owner, Ashietu Adams, was said to have fled. The Deputy Director in charge of the Pharmaceutical Division, Investigation and Enforcement Directorate, NAFDAC, Pharm. Edith Joseph, who spoke during an inspection of the facility said the agency received intelligence on October 16 concerning the alleged production of Aishetu Adams Bitters with a fake NAFDAC registration number, prompting surveillance and intelligence gathering that led to the discovery of the facility concealed inside a residential building. “What we found was shocking. The facility was in a very poor and unhygienic condition. Look at the water they use for production and the environment where the manufacturing takes place. The products are manufactured outdoors, in the open air. I can tell you that this facility is not approved by NAFDAC,” she said. The products recovered were identified as Ashietu Adams Herbal Mixture for sexually transmitted diseases, Ashietu Adams Blood Purifier and another herbal preparation purportedly used for high blood pressure. Joseph said none of the three products was registered with NAFDAC, adding that the registration number displayed on the blood purifier belonged to a registered cough syrup. “The number belongs to another registered product, which is a cough syrup. They simply copied the number and placed it on their product to deceive Nigerians,” she said. According to her, the products were manufactured without regulatory approval, while their packaging lacked the manufacturer’s name and a verifiable address to establish their origin. She said the agency had sealed the facility pending further investigation and taken the recovered products to its office. Joseph disclosed that Sayidu claimed to have worked with Adams for about a year and assisted in managing the business, particularly when she travelled. The manager reportedly told officials that Adams, whom he identified as a Ghanaian woman, had travelled to Ghana. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Chioma obinna The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control (NAFDAC) on Thursday uncovered another illegal herbal products factory in Agege, Lagos, where three unregistered products were allegedly manufactured under unhygienic conditions, with one bearing a registration number belonging to a registered cough syrup. The agency sealed the facility, evacuated the products and arrested the manager, identified as Abulaziz Sayidu, for interrogation, while the alleged owner, Ashietu Adams, was said to have fled. The Deputy Director in charge of the Pharmaceutical Division, Investigation and Enforcement Directorate, NAFDAC, Pharm. Edith Joseph, who spoke during an inspection of the facility said the agency received intelligence on October 16 concerning the alleged production of Aishetu Adams Bitters with a fake NAFDAC registration number, prompting surveillance and intelligence gathering that led to the discovery of the facility concealed inside a residential building. “What we found was shocking. The facility was in a very poor and unhygienic condition. Look at the water they use for production and the environment where the manufacturing takes place. The products are manufactured outdoors, in the open air. I can tell you that this facility is not approved by NAFDAC,” she said. The products recovered were identified as Ashietu Adams Herbal Mixture for sexually transmitted diseases, Ashietu Adams Blood Purifier and another herbal preparation purportedly used for high blood pressure. Joseph said none of the three products was registered with NAFDAC, adding that the registration number displayed on the blood purifier belonged to a registered cough syrup. “The number belongs to another registered product, which is a cough syrup. They simply copied the number and placed it on their product to deceive Nigerians,” she said. According to her, the products were manufactured without regulatory approval, while their packaging lacked the manufacturer’s name and a verifiable address to establish their origin. She said the agency had sealed the facility pending further investigation and taken the recovered products to its office. Joseph disclosed that Sayidu claimed to have worked with Adams for about a year and assisted in managing the business, particularly when she travelled. The manager reportedly told officials that Adams, whom he identified as a Ghanaian woman, had travelled to Ghana. The agency said investigations were ongoing to establish the circumstances surrounding the operation and the whereabouts of the alleged owner. NAFDAC WARNS CONSUMERS Joseph warned Nigerians against relying solely on NAFDAC registration numbers when purchasing herbal medicines and other regulated products, noting that counterfeiters could copy legitimate numbers to give unregistered products the appearance of regulatory approval. She advised consumers to verify product details through NAFDAC’s online verification platforms and the agency’s Greenbook. “If the name displayed does not match the product being presented, consumers should know that something is wrong,” she said. She urged consumers, particularly those in rural communities with limited internet access, to visit the nearest NAFDAC office for assistance in verifying the authenticity of products before purchase or consumption. The deputy director identified the absence of a valid registration number, manufacturer’s name and verifiable address as major warning signs, adding that the agency was intensifying surveillance and enforcement operations against illegal manufacturing outlets. Also speaking during the inspection, Deputy Director of Public Relations, NAFDAC, Mrs Christiana Obiazikwor, called for increased public participation in the fight against counterfeit and unregistered products. Obiazikwor warned landlords and property owners against allowing their premises to be used for illegal manufacturing activities, noting that those found to be aiding criminal operations could face prosecution. She urged property owners to monitor activities on their premises and report suspicious operations to the appropriate authorities. “We cannot fight this battle alone. Every Nigerian has a role to play in identifying and reporting places where illegal manufacturing activities are taking place,” she said. Obiazikwor said NAFDAC was expanding public awareness through radio programmes, multilingual jingles and community sensitisation campaigns, including its “NAFDAC and Your Health” programme. She said the agency also conducted awareness campaigns in local government areas, churches and schools to educate Nigerians on how to identify suspicious products and report illegal manufacturing activities. Emphasising the importance of product traceability, she said consumers should check details such as the manufacturer’s address and batch number rather than relying solely on a registration number. “These products do not have batch numbers or the manufacturer’s address. These are important details that help establish the identity and traceability of a product,” she said. She added that the agency was working towards stiffer penalties for offences involving the manufacture and distribution of counterfeit and unregistered products. NAFDAC urged members of the public to report suspected illegal manufacturing activities, assuring them that reports would be handled discreetly. The post NAFDAC uncovers another fake herbal factory in Lagos, arrests manager appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Lawal swears in five permanent secretaries
item.description: — Charges appointees to uphold public service rules, financial regulations By Idris Salisu GUSAU — Zamfara State Governor, Dauda Lawal, has sworn in five new permanent secretaries into the state civil service, charging them to comply with public service rules, financial regulations and other relevant laws. The swearing-in ceremony took place on Thursday at the Grand Chamber of the Government House in Gusau, with the Chief Judge of the state, Justice Kulu Aliyu, administering the oath of office. The new permanent secretaries are Ahmad S. Zamfara, Nasiru Halilu Anka, Mu’azu Jibril Guraguri, Adamu Abdullahi Kanoma and Sani Muhammad Shinkafi. Speaking at the ceremony, Lawal said the appointments reflected confidence in the officers’ experience, abilities and readiness to assume greater responsibilities in the state’s administration. He said permanent secretaries played a critical role in providing administrative leadership, ensuring institutional continuity, advising on policy implementation and maintaining discipline within the civil service. “Becoming permanent secretaries is more than personal advancement: as senior administrative leaders, your decisions and conduct directly affect government performance and the welfare of the people we serve,” the governor said. Lawal said his administration remained committed to strengthening government institutions and improving public administration to support the state’s development agenda. He urged the appointees to ensure that government policies were backed by proper planning, realistic implementation strategies, effective supervision and continuous assessment of results. “Proper planning, realistic implementation strategies, effective supervision and continuous assessment of results must support policies and programmes,” he said. The governor also advised the permanent secretaries to maintain professional relationships with commissioners and other political officeholders, stressing the need for cooperation between political leaders and career civil servants. “Political leaders set policy; career civil servants provide the institutional knowledge, technical advice, and administrative capacity to implement it. These roles complement each other, and the effectiveness of the government depends on mutual respect,” he said. Lawal said the civil service remained central to translating government decisions into tangible results, particularly in the delivery of essential services and the implementation of reforms aimed at meeting the needs and aspirations of Zamfara residents. He urged the new permanent secretaries to approach their assignments with discipline, professionalism and a clear understanding of the administration’s priorities. The post Lawal swears in five permanent secretaries appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ebola: FG quarantines high-risk contacts, says no evidence of community transmission yet
item.description: …allays fears of spread . ..Patient recovering, says minister …States, hospitals step up preparedness By Chioma Obinna & Chidinma Chukwu The Federal Government on Thursday said it has intensified efforts to contain Nigeria’s confirmed case of Ebola Virus Disease; place high-risk contacts in quarantine isolate other contacts and strengthened preparedness across states as well as health facilities. The government also allayed fears of a wider outbreak even as it also announced that the index patient was showing significant signs of recovery, while stressing that there was, so far, no evidence that the infection had spread into the community. Briefing journalists on the national response in Abuja, the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof Ali Pate said the government was working to prevent further transmission through contact tracing, surveillance and coordinated emergency measures. “I spoke with the clinicians today, and I understand that the laboratory results show significant improvement. There is a possibility that she will recover fully. However, we cannot take anything for granted,” the minister said. “We currently have one confirmed case, and our priority is to contain it and prevent transmission into communities or a wider outbreak. We are working very hard to ensure that this does not happen.” The Minister explained that the case was imported based on the patient’s travel history, noting that she was asymptomatic when she arrived in Nigeria but developed symptoms a few days later. Following confirmation of the infection, public health authorities immediately commenced contact tracing, covering people at the hospital where she received treatment, her domestic contacts and a private medical facility she had visited. He said contacts had been categorised according to their levels of exposure, with high-risk contacts placed in quarantine at a designated facility and others isolated in line with public health guidelines. He explained that that Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has activated its incident management system and is coordinating the day-to-day national response in collaboration with the Federal Capital Territory Administration, where the case was identified. The minister, however, warned that the improving condition of the patient and the absence of evidence of community transmission should not lead to complacency. “We remain vigilant and are not taking anything for granted. However, there is no need for panic. We are confident that we can manage the situation, but we need the cooperation of Nigerians,” he said. There is a possibility that she will recover fully. However, we cannot take anything for granted,” the minister said. “We currently have one confirmed case, and our priority is to contain it and prevent transmission into communities or a wider outbreak. We are working very hard to ensure that this does not happen.” The Minister explained that the case was imported based on the patient’s travel history, noting that she was asymptomatic when she arrived in Nigeria but developed symptoms a few days later. Following confirmation of the infection, public health authorities immediately commenced contact tracing, covering people at the hospital where she received treatment, her domestic contacts and a private medical facility she had visited. He said contacts had been categorised according to their levels of exposure, with high-risk contacts placed in quarantine at a designated facility and others isolated in line with public health guidelines. He explained that that Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has activated its incident management system and is coordinating the day-to-day national response in collaboration with the Federal Capital Territory Administration, where the case was identified. The minister, however, warned that the improving condition of the patient and the absence of evidence of community transmission should not lead to complacency. “We remain vigilant and are not taking anything for granted. However, there is no need for panic. We are confident that we can manage the situation, but we need the cooperation of Nigerians,” he said. FG mobilises states, resources As part of efforts to prevent a wider outbreak, the Federal Government said it had informed all state governments and directed those yet to complete their Ebola response plans to do so urgently. The minister disclosed that the government had mobilised additional resources for the response, including funds released by President Bola Tinubu to strengthen the capacity of the NCDC. He said the Presidential Task Force had been briefed, alongside the Nigeria Governors’ Forum and the National Economic Council, chaired by the Vice-President. “All state governments have been informed. Most states already have response plans developed with the guidance of the NCDC. We have directed those that are yet to complete their plans to do so urgently,” he said. The government is also adopting a whole-of-government approach involving the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the Ministry of Aviation and other relevant agencies. The minister said a meeting with state commissioners of health and information was scheduled to strengthen coordination and ensure that public communication remained consistent across the country. He maintained that Nigeria’s public health system had demonstrated its capacity to respond swiftly, noting that authorities diagnosed and confirmed the case within 24 hours of notification and informed the World Health Organisation (WHO). “We are not starting from scratch,” he said, expressing confidence in the expertise of Nigerian health professionals and the investments made in public health preparedness. Experts to sequence virus The government has also initiated steps to sequence the virus’s genome to improve understanding of the strain involved and support the response. The minister said Professor Christian Happi, a renowned infectious disease genomics expert based at Redeemer University, Ede, had been invited to complement the work of the NCDC through the African Centre of Excellence for Genomics of Infectious Diseases. He said international partners, including WHO and the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, were supporting the response, while experts with experience in managing outbreaks in other countries had arrived to assist Nigeria. The minister said the collaboration demonstrated the importance of strengthening local expertise and scientific capacity in responding to public health emergencies. FG steps up border screening The government also announced plans to intensify screening and preventive measures at Nigeria’s points of entry as part of efforts to reduce the risk of further imported infections. According to the minister, port health services had been strengthened, while additional capacity was being sought to improve screening and ensure that thermal imaging equipment was functional. He said the assessment of travellers would continue to be guided by risk categorisation and international health regulations. The minister disclosed that Nigeria had gone five months without recording a case despite substantial international travel, with more than 40,000 travellers entering the country during that period. He said the government would continue to strengthen border health measures, but stressed that the immediate priority remained containing the confirmed case and tracing all contacts. Hospitals, private clinics on alert Further, the Ali Pate said all federal hospitals had been notified and directed to ensure adequate bed capacity, functional isolation facilities and strict infection prevention and control measures. State governments were also urged to prepare their hospitals and ensure that health workers were trained and adequately equipped to identify and manage suspected cases. He particularly emphasised the role of private healthcare providers, noting that the patient had visited a private medical facility before the infection was confirmed. “The private sector is equally important because the patient visited a private health facility. A similar situation occurred during Nigeria’s 2014 Ebola response,” he said. He called for closer collaboration between private medical practitioners and public health authorities to ensure that suspected cases were promptly reported and managed according to established protocols. The government urged anyone who develops symptoms such as fever, headaches or muscle aches, particularly with a relevant travel history or possible exposure, to promptly contact public health authorities for guidance. The minister also advised Nigerians to practise frequent handwashing and avoid unnecessary contact with other people’s body fluids. “Ebola is not an airborne disease. It is transmitted through direct contact with infected body fluids,” he said, urging health workers and members of the public to follow expert advice. No immediate cancellation of public events On whether conferences, campaigns and other large public gatherings scheduled for the coming days would be cancelled, the minister said the government was monitoring the situation and would base any decision on scientific evidence and expert advice. “At this time, there is no indication that we need to change plans for large gatherings that have already been scheduled,” he said. item.title: Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night' depicts the sky on July 22, 1889, researchers find
item.description: null Researchers think they might have pinpointed the exact night sky that we see depicted in Vincent van Gogh's iconic painting "The Starry Night." Perhaps one of the most famous paintings in modern history, Van Gogh's "The Starry Night" carries a legacy that continues to inspire and mystify generation after generation. But while you might see in its swirls of color and bright spots of starlight a night sky derived purely from imagination, some scientists think it represents an actual view — one that includes a waning crescent moon, Venus and the Hyades cluster. And they may know exactly when this sky appeared.. In a new study, researchers suggest that "The Starry Night" depicts the pre-dawn sky seen around July 22, 1889 from Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, where Van Gogh painted it. But while this sky happens to perfectly match the one depicted in the artwork, art historians have long thought that Van Gogh painted this piece in June. Could these findings shift the date of this legendary artwork? Finding a painted sky This investigation started decades ago with art historian Albert Boime and astronomer George Abell at UCLA in 1984 and continued in the following years with astronomer Charles Whitney at Harvard University. However, these earlier analyses did not agree with one another, and there was no true consensus about exactly when the sky matched with the painting. So the question remained, lingering in the minds of those with a shared love for both art and space. And a team led by Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim, the CEO of South Korean robotic telescope company SLLAB and a Ph.D. candidate at Kyung Hee University's School of Space Research, picked up the search once more. "When they see a fragment of a starry sky, observational astronomers like me and amateur astronomers alike will want to solve the puzzle. I am simply someone who pursued that process a little more actively," Kim told Space.com . A figure from Kim et al.'s paper in Scientific Reports. According to the figure: "The central cluster of stars in The Starry Night (1889), left, and the Hyades cluster in Taurus, center. At right, the five stars in the painting (orange) are overlaid on the real stars (blue) after matching for size, orientation and position; red dashed lines show the residual differences."
