item.dc:creator: Chelsea Gohd
item.content:encoded: null Researchers think they might have pinpointed the exact night sky that we see depicted in Vincent van Gogh's iconic painting "The Starry Night." Perhaps one of the most famous paintings in modern history, Van Gogh's "The Starry Night" carries a legacy that continues to inspire and mystify generation after generation. But while you might see in its swirls of color and bright spots of starlight a night sky derived purely from imagination, some scientists think it represents an actual view — one that includes a waning crescent moon, Venus and the Hyades cluster. And they may know exactly when this sky appeared.. In a new study, researchers suggest that "The Starry Night" depicts the pre-dawn sky seen around July 22, 1889 from Saint-Rémy-de-Provence, where Van Gogh painted it. But while this sky happens to perfectly match the one depicted in the artwork, art historians have long thought that Van Gogh painted this piece in June. Could these findings shift the date of this legendary artwork? Finding a painted sky This investigation started decades ago with art historian Albert Boime and astronomer George Abell at UCLA in 1984 and continued in the following years with astronomer Charles Whitney at Harvard University. However, these earlier analyses did not agree with one another, and there was no true consensus about exactly when the sky matched with the painting. So the question remained, lingering in the minds of those with a shared love for both art and space. And a team led by Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim, the CEO of South Korean robotic telescope company SLLAB and a Ph.D. candidate at Kyung Hee University's School of Space Research, picked up the search once more. "When they see a fragment of a starry sky, observational astronomers like me and amateur astronomers alike will want to solve the puzzle. I am simply someone who pursued that process a little more actively," Kim told Space.com . A figure from Kim et al.'s paper in Scientific Reports. According to the figure: "The central cluster of stars in The Starry Night (1889), left, and the Hyades cluster in Taurus, center. At right, the five stars in the painting (orange) are overlaid on the real stars (blue) after matching for size, orientation and position; red dashed lines show the residual differences." (Image credit: Kim et al., Scientific Reports (2026)) But how did Kim's team come to their conclusion, after others had failed to nail down a date over the decades? In short, "we analyzed the painting astronomically, analyzed documents about his situation in July 1889, and then carried out ecological and meteorological investigations," Kim said. To start with, the team analyzed the sky from the exact location in Saint-Rémy where Van Gogh is said to have painted "The Starry Night." They then used observational geometry to map the historical night sky. "Modern telescopes are equipped with a function called astrometry, which compares an image of the night sky with celestial coordinates stored in a computer and automatically extracts the coordinates of the image," Kim said. "We used Procrustes analysis, a method that compares only the 'shape' of two sets of points. After matching their position, size and rotation, it measures how similar the two shapes are from the differences that remain (the residuals)." "Because a star cluster on the canvas may be larger or smaller than in reality and slightly tilted, this method was the right fit. It allowed us to explain, in quantitative terms, what earlier studies had described only qualitatively as 'resembling a certain constellation,'" Kim added. But this quantitative analysis wasn't enough to say for sure that this was the right-fitting sky, as different constellations could fit to a similar degree, Kim explained. To get closer to their answer, the team combined their analysis with a deep dive through history. "We also checked whether the stars were actually in that part of the pre-dawn sky on that date, whether they fall within the painter’s field of view, and whether the appearance of the moon and Venus matches the painting. It was the Hyades that satisfied all of these conditions," Kim said. Exploring astro-art history As mentioned, the date of this matching sky comes in late July, a month after art historians think Van Gogh painted "The Starry Night." But the researchers suggest that their findings could provide evidence to support the idea that the work was actually painted in July. Letters written by Van Gogh as early as 1888 describe his desire to paint a star-filled sky. A letter dated April 12, 1888 reads: "A starry sky, for example, well — it’s a thing that I’d like to try to do, just as in the daytime I’ll try to paint a green meadow studded with dandelions." Kim followed these letters through the months to try and find more information that could potentially alleviate the discrepancy between the matching skies and the actual month the painting was created. Kim pointed to a letter from between late May and early June 1889 that reads: "This morning I saw the countryside from my window a long time before sunrise with nothing but the morning star, which looked very big." Kim drew on "personal imagination" to find ties between Van Gogh's sky observations in these months and what they might mean for the painting's timeline, Kim shared, so this doesn't definitively change the view of this painting's history. However, Kim suggested that these records could indicate that Van Gogh was repeatedly looking up and watching the pre-dawn sky, which could have led to him seeing this exact sky on July 22. The painting itself even ignites uncertainty among art historians. As the researchers cite in their new paper, leading art historians see "The Starry Night" as stylistically different from Van Gogh's other works during the month of June, drawing further questions over the date painted. "What our study shows is that the sky in the painting matches, in both observation and shape, the real pre-dawn sky around July 22. So, what we propose is the possibility that Vincent conceived the idea in June and completed the painting after July 22," Kim said. However, "I think further research in art history and conservation science could shed more light on this question," Kim added. This work was described in a study published Oct. 22 in the journal Scientific Reports.

item.title: Video: If they can jump, vote for them — Makinde tells supporters
item.description: Presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde has challenged Nigerians to assess the energy and stamina of candidates seeking to lead the country in the 2027 presidential election. Makinde spoke on Thursday at the South-West town hall meeting of the Makinde/Daura campaign organisation in Akure, the Ondo State capital. He said he would not make age an issue in the presidential contest but would rather focus on candidates’ physical energy and ability to cope with the demands of the office. To demonstrate his point, the governor jumped off the stage and challenged other presidential candidates to perform the same feat. APM presidential candidate Seyi Makinde leapt off the stage during a town hall, challenging supporters to vote for the opposition if their candidates could pull off the same stunt. Video Credit : Channels Television // X pic.twitter.com/nvGIuNNd0b — Vanguard Newspapers (@vanguardngrnews) October 22, 2026 “When they bring their presidential candidate, let the candidate come here and also jump down,” he said. “If they can do that, vote for them.” Makinde also defended his decision to contest the presidency despite President Bola Tinubu, who is also from the South-West, seeking re-election in 2027. He argued that the region’s support for a presidential candidate should not prevent other qualified candidates from the same geopolitical zone from contesting. “I’ve listened to people who asked us why we are contesting in this election when the south-west already has somebody sitting on that seat, and I’ve explained to them that we have an example here in the south-west,” he said. The governor cited the 1999 presidential election, when former President Olusegun Obasanjo and Olu Falae, both from the South-West, contested against each other. “In 1999, the entire Nigeria ceded the presidency to the South-West, and we had two of our fathers, Baba President Obasanjo and Baba Olu Falae, contest the presidency, both from the south-west. And heaven did not fall,” he said. “As a matter of fact, what the south-west did was to present two of its finest, two of its best, for Nigeria to choose from. Is there anything wrong with us this time around?” Makinde also urged people in the South-West to reject what he described as the politics of deceit, accusing the Tinubu administration of wasting taxpayers’ money. He specifically criticised Jimoh Ibrahim, Nigeria’s permanent representative to the United Nations, over his trip from New York to Abuja to present the UN budget to Tinubu. The governor questioned the need for the trip, arguing that the Federal Government had yet to clarify which national budget it was implementing. “Well, they can waste the taxpayers’ money, but I refuse to agree that you must use the taxpayers’ money to fly from New York to Abuja to present the UN budget when, indeed, this is an administration where, right now, we don’t know which budget they are operating on for Nigeria,” he said. “Is it the 2023, 2024,

item.title: Forgotten Pokémon Card Collection Goes for $2 Million
item.description: The Pokémon TCG collector scene has taken off in recent years, with particularly sought-after cards fetching obscene prices . However, despite its reputation as a niche space for hardcore collectors, the latest winner of the Pokémon sweepstakes doesn’t fit the usual profile. A British retiree just became a millionaire after auctioning off his forgotten Pokémon card collection, which had been gathering dust in his attic.

item.title: Fernandes to remain Man Utd captain despite outburst
item.description: … as Rooney brands players ‘selfish’ and ‘babies’ By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes will not be disciplined for his post-match criticism of head coach Michael Carrick following the club’s 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, while former striker Wayne Rooney has branded the players “selfish” and “babies”. According to the BBC, Fernandes will retain the captaincy despite questioning Carrick’s tactics after Wednesday’s damaging defeat in Italy, which intensified concerns over United’s performances and the manager’s future. The Portugal international criticised the team’s tactical approach and said it was the responsibility of Carrick and his coaching staff, rather than the players, to identify problems and make the necessary changes. His comments were widely viewed as a challenge to Carrick’s authority, coming just eight days after defender Lisandro Martinez criticised director of football Jason Wilcox and the club’s summer recruitment. However, there is sympathy within Old Trafford for Fernandes, who conducted 10 post-match interviews despite being substituted for Joshua Zirkzee midway through the second half. Although some of his remarks have disappointed the club, his frustration is understood given the scale of United’s defeat. It remains unclear whether Fernandes will feature in Sunday’s Premier League match against Bournemouth. Carrick is expected to address the issue at his pre-match news conference on Friday. Rooney slams ‘selfish’ Man Utd players Rooney said he was in “shock” and “disbelief” at United’s performance against Como, adding that he was as worried about the club’s situation as he had been “for a long time”. Speaking on the United Stand podcast, the former United and England captain said the public criticism from Martinez and Fernandes showed players were shifting blame instead of accepting responsibility. “When Martinez came out, I said this is an absolute nightmare because it will rip the dressing room apart,” Rooney said. “That was the start. We’ve seen it now with Bruno and you’re going to see it with more players because they don’t want to take responsibility.” He added: “These players, they’re selfish. They don’t care about their team-mates, don’t care about the manager, the staff or the fans, they care about themselves. If they’re not getting what’s right for them, they’re like babies and just throw their toys out of the pram and go and deflect the blame on to anyone else but themselves.” Rooney also argued that Fernandes, whose form has declined from last season when he won the PFA and FWA Player of the Year awards and set a Premier League assists record, needed to examine his own performances. “If he looks at himself in the mirror, if Martinez and all of them looked at themselves in the mirror, they’ll find what’s looking back at them is them, and that’s not good enough. Rooney urges Carrick to fight for his job Rooney has also called on United’s board to clarify Carrick’s future, insisting the head coach must stand up for himself amid growing pressure. item.title: APC Campaign Council: Atiku politicising Ebola outbreak, ₦10bn emergency fund remains untouched
item.description: — defends surveillance measures The All Progressives Congress (APC) Presidential Campaign Council has accused former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar of politicising Nigeria’s Ebola response, saying the ₦10 billion approved by President Bola Tinubu for the emergency in June 2026 remains untouched. The council, in a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday by its spokesperson, Dele Alake, also defended the government’s handling of the public health concern, saying the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC), the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria (FAAN) and other agencies had been using existing resources for surveillance activities. The statement followed comments attributed to Atiku questioning the utilisation of the ₦10 billion Ebola emergency fund and criticising the government’s response to the reported case involving a Nigerian who travelled from Uganda. The APC council faulted the framing of Atiku’s statement, arguing that linking President Tinubu’s name to Ebola risked turning a serious public health concern into a political attack. It also said the incubation period for Ebola ranges from two to 21 days, with symptoms typically appearing eight to 10 days after exposure, adding that infected persons generally become capable of transmitting the virus after symptoms develop. According to the council, the infected Nigerian reported to a hospital days after the initial exposure, where several tests confirmed the infection. On the emergency fund, the council said the ₦10 billion approved by Tinubu in June had not been utilised, as the agencies involved were drawing on other available resources to conduct surveillance and related activities. It praised the agencies for what it described as a robust surveillance network at Nigeria’s entry points, saying the system helped alert authorities to the reported case and facilitated contact tracing involving 44 contacts of the patient. The council argued that the opposition should support public health authorities rather than criticise the government over the response. It also rejected an allegation attributed to Atiku’s camp that a ministerial briefing on Ebola was intended to discourage attendance at campaign rallies or voting, describing the claim as speculative and demanding verifiable evidence. According to the statement, the briefing did not raise such an issue but appealed to Nigerians to comply with protocols announced by the Presidential Task Force. The council urged Atiku and his supporters to avoid politicising public health issues, calling on Nigerians across party lines to support health authorities, communicate responsibly and comply with preventive measures. “A time like this demands that all Nigerians, including the opposition, rally around the health authorities and professionals, communicate responsibly, avoid rumour-mongering, and follow the protocols advised by the Task Force to ensure Ebola does not become a national epidemic,” the statement said. item.title: Makinde Rallies South-West To Lead Nigeria’s Rebirth
item.description: Oyo State Governor and Allied Peoples’ Movement (APM) presidential candidate, Seyi Makinde, has urged the Southwest to lead Nigeria’s national rebirth, calling on the region to reject entitlement, nepotism and “turn-by-turn” politics. Makinde made the call on Thursday at the APM Southwest Town Hall held at the Ondo State International Conference Centre, The Dome, in Akure, where he presented his Reset Nigeria agenda as a pathway to national renewal. He described the Southwest as a historic vanguard of Nigeria’s progress, arguing that the region must once again take the lead in shaping the country’s political and economic future. The governor dismissed suggestions that the Southwest should not produce another presidential candidate because the region currently holds the presidency. He cited the 1999 presidential election, when former President Olusegun Obasanjo and Olu Falae contested for the country’s highest office without controversy. Makinde at the APM South West Town Hall Meeting in Akure on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Facebook/Seyi Makinde. According to him, leadership should be determined by competence, energy and readiness to serve, rather than claims of entitlement to political office. Makinde outlined four pillars of his Reset Nigeria agenda: education, the economy, security and sociopolitical empowerment. He said Nigeria’s prosperity depends on a skilled and knowledgeable population, a secure environment and a political system that allows the opposition to thrive. On the economy, Makinde criticised what he described as a lack of clarity in the Federal Government’s budgeting process, contrasting it with Oyo State’s January-to-December budget cycle and more than 70 per cent budget performance over the past seven years. He called for a productive economy in which states receive their statutory allocations without delay and taxation is designed to promote prosperity rather than deepen poverty. Makinde also urged supporters to become “Reset Agents”, obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and take the party’s message to households across the country. He insisted that the Southwest must reclaim its place at the forefront of national transformation, declaring, “Together, we will reset Nigeria.” The APM vice-presidential candidate, Alhaji Lawal Daura, reaffirmed the party’s commitment to national renewal and cautioned members against what he described as political infiltration aimed at creating divisions within its ranks. He maintained that the party remained united and resolute in its mission. The APM vice-presidential candidate, Alhaji Lawal Daura, at the APM South West Town Hall Meeting in Akure on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Facebook/Seyi Makinde. In goodwill messages, former Osun State Governor, Prince Olagunsoye Oyinlola; APM Deputy Director-General (Administration), Hajia Maryam Inna Ciroma; and retired civil servant, Dr Layi Ogunbambi, commended Makinde’s courage and urged Nigerian youths to support leaders they described as visionary

The governor dismissed suggestions that the Southwest should not produce another presidential candidate because the region currently holds the presidency. He cited the 1999 presidential election, when former President Olusegun Obasanjo and Olu Falae contested for the country’s highest office without controversy. Makinde at the APM South West Town Hall Meeting in Akure on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Facebook/Seyi Makinde. According to him, leadership should be determined by competence, energy and readiness to serve, rather than claims of entitlement to political office. Makinde outlined four pillars of his Reset Nigeria agenda: education, the economy, security and sociopolitical empowerment. He said Nigeria’s prosperity depends on a skilled and knowledgeable population, a secure environment and a political system that allows the opposition to thrive. On the economy, Makinde criticised what he described as a lack of clarity in the Federal Government’s budgeting process, contrasting it with Oyo State’s January-to-December budget cycle and more than 70 per cent budget performance over the past seven years. He called for a productive economy in which states receive their statutory allocations without delay and taxation is designed to promote prosperity rather than deepen poverty. Makinde also urged supporters to become “Reset Agents”, obtain their Permanent Voter Cards (PVCs) and take the party’s message to households across the country. He insisted that the Southwest must reclaim its place at the forefront of national transformation, declaring, “Together, we will reset Nigeria.” The APM vice-presidential candidate, Alhaji Lawal Daura, reaffirmed the party’s commitment to national renewal and cautioned members against what he described as political infiltration aimed at creating divisions within its ranks. The APM vice-presidential candidate, Alhaji Lawal Daura, at the APM South West Town Hall Meeting in Akure on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Facebook/Seyi Makinde. In goodwill messages, former Osun State Governor, Prince Olagunsoye Oyinlola; APM Deputy Director-General (Administration), Hajia Maryam Inna Ciroma; and retired civil servant, Dr Layi Ogunbambi, commended Makinde’s courage and urged Nigerian youths to support leaders they described as visionary and energetic. The party’s National Chairman, Alhaji Yusuf Dantalle, and National Leader, Senator Bala Mohammed, criticised the ruling party’s economic policies, arguing that they had worsened hardship across the country. They expressed confidence in the Makinde-Daura ticket, saying the APM could restore economic prosperity and reset the country if elected in 2027. Earlier, the Southwest Zonal Coordinator of the Makinde-Daura Campaign Organisation, Chief Eddy Olafeso, said responsible governance must put the people first, adding that Makinde was prepared to redefine leadership and reset Nigeria. Those at the event included Oyo State Deputy Governor, Barrister Bayo Lawal; former Deputy Governor, Engineer Hamid Gbadamosi; Speaker of the Oyo State House of Assembly, Adebo Ogundoyin; former Speaker and Senator, Monsurat Sunmonu; and other key stakeholders from the Southwest. item.title: Scientists turned art detectives date van Gogh's 'Starry Night' to actual night sky in 1889
item.description: A team of South Korean researchers has put forward a new date for the night sky depicted in Dutch painter Vincent van Gogh's famed masterpiece "The Starry Night". Art historians have long assumed the stars were a product of the artist's fantasy or dated the scene to June 1889 based on the artist's known location and other factors, but astronomical details like the sliver crescent moon didn't line up.

item.title: NEC Endorses 90-Day Economic Plan To Ease Cost Of Living For Nigerians
item.description: The National Economic Council (NEC) has endorsed a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate the gains of President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, with a focus on reducing the cost of living and improving food affordability. The plan also prioritises attracting investment, removing bottlenecks to economic activities and accelerating the completion of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians. According to a statement by Stanley Nkwocha, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Communications in the Office of the Vice President, the endorsement followed a presentation by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, at NEC’s 161st meeting held virtually on Thursday and chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima. The five priority areas identified in the plan are food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support. 161st NEC meeting on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency NEC also approved the establishment of a national dashboard to track ongoing projects across the federation, with emphasis on transparency, accountability and accurate reporting on the utilisation of proceeds from fuel subsidy removal. Presenting the economic outlook, Oyedele expressed optimism about progress under the Tinubu administration’s reform programme and the prospects for further economic recovery. He identified reducing headline inflation and interest rates to single digits by 2027 as key policy objectives, noting that the next phase of reforms would require coordinated implementation across federal and state institutions. The presentation also highlighted the need to translate macroeconomic improvements into measurable benefits for households and businesses through targeted interventions, improved fiscal coordination and the removal of barriers to investment. Addressing Council members, Shettima said that although President Tinubu’s economic reforms were designed to achieve broader national prosperity, governments at all levels must ensure that the objectives translate into improved living conditions for Nigerians. He charged state governors and relevant institutions to focus on affordable transportation, improved healthcare, employment opportunities and greater financial security. “The first dividend of prosperity should be the confidence to plan a life. Our task is to make such confidence less dependent on fortune,” he said. Shettima described the Council’s deliberations on transportation, healthcare, police reform and livestock development as critical to determining the quality of life Nigerians should expect from economic progress. item.dc:creator: Donatus Anichukwueze
item.content:encoded: The National Economic Council (NEC) has endorsed a 90-day economic action plan proposed by the Federal Ministry of Finance to consolidate the gains of President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, with a focus on reducing the cost of living and improving food affordability. The plan also prioritises attracting investment, removing bottlenecks to economic activities and accelerating the completion of projects with direct benefits to Nigerians. According to a statement by Stanley Nkwocha, Senior Special Assistant to the President on Media and Communications in the Office of the Vice President, the endorsement followed a presentation by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Taiwo Oyedele, at NEC’s 161st meeting held virtually on Thursday and chaired by Vice President Kashim Shettima. The five priority areas identified in the plan are food affordability, tax harmonisation, completion of high-impact projects, resolution of investment bottlenecks and regulated household support. 161st NEC meeting on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency NEC also approved the establishment of a national dashboard to track ongoing projects across the federation, with emphasis on transparency, accountability and accurate reporting on the utilisation of proceeds from fuel subsidy removal. Presenting the economic outlook, Oyedele expressed optimism about progress under the Tinubu administration’s reform programme and the prospects for further economic recovery. He identified reducing headline inflation and interest rates to single digits by 2027 as key policy objectives, noting that the next phase of reforms would require coordinated implementation across federal and state institutions. The presentation also highlighted the need to translate macroeconomic improvements into measurable benefits for households and businesses through targeted interventions, improved fiscal coordination and the removal of barriers to investment. Addressing Council members, Shettima said that although President Tinubu’s economic reforms were designed to achieve broader national prosperity, governments at all levels must ensure that the objectives translate into improved living conditions for Nigerians. He charged state governors and relevant institutions to focus on affordable transportation, improved healthcare, employment opportunities and greater financial security. “The first dividend of prosperity should be the confidence to plan a life. Our task is to make such confidence less dependent on fortune,” he said. Shettima described the Council’s deliberations on transportation, healthcare, police reform and livestock development as critical to determining the quality of life Nigerians should expect from economic progress. VP Shettima chairing 161st NEC meeting held virtually on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency “Our separate jurisdictions must serve a common public interest,” he said, stressing that Nigeria’s federal structure should strengthen cooperation rather than hinder the delivery of essential services. On the National Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Bus Initiative, the Vice President urged state governments to support affordable transportation systems that would ease the financial burden on commuters. He said the programme’s success should be measured by affordability and accessibility rather than the number of vehicles deployed. “The cost of reaching a livelihood should never consume the livelihood itself. The passenger’s experience must guide our ambition, because the value of public transport resides in the journeys it makes possible. We should assess success through affordability and access, rather than fleet size alone,” he said. Shettima urged governors to bring their knowledge of local conditions into national policy decisions, adding that effective implementation required clear responsibilities and practical agreements among the tiers of government. “Our separate mandates must not become competing excuses. Each Governor carries knowledge that no federal document can supply,” he said. He added that every policy proposal should be assessed by its ability to reduce uncertainty, create opportunities and strengthen public confidence in government. “Nigerians deserve institutions on which they can organise their lives. Providing that assurance is among the most consequential uses of public authority. That is the assurance we owe them,” he said. VP Shettima chairing 161st NEC meeting held virtually on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency NEC Reviews Ebola Response, Tasks States On Preparedness Meanwhile, NEC received an update from the Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Prof. Muhammad Ali Pate, on the reported Ebola outbreak in the Federal Capital Territory. Pate allayed fears of a major public health crisis, assuring Council members that Nigeria had the institutional capacity to contain the situation. He outlined efforts by the ministry and relevant stakeholders to establish a robust national response system, identifying coordination and governance, detection at points of entry, laboratory testing, logistics for essential kits and personal protective equipment, and strategic communication as critical components. The minister said 21 state governments had updated their response plans and urged the remaining 15 states to establish appropriate preparedness and response mechanisms without delay. NEC Directs States To Strengthen Polio Eradication Efforts Council also received the report of the NEC Ad Hoc Committee on Polio Eradication, chaired by Gombe State Governor, Muhammadu Inuwa Yahaya. It resolved to direct states to conduct post-campaign reviews, particularly in areas where children were missed during immunisation exercises and communities affected by insecurity. VP Shettima chairing 161st NEC meeting held virtually on Thursday, October 22, 2026. Photo credit: Presidency NEC stressed the need for timely release of counterpart funds, stronger routine immunisation, improved coordination with security agencies and closer cooperation among states to improve coverage in subsequent campaigns. It also emphasised that sustained political commitment from governors, traditional rulers and security agencies would remain critical to eradicating polio in Nigeria. NEC Moves To Unlock Livestock Sector’s Economic Potential On livestock development, Council received the report of its Ad Hoc Committee on Livestock Development, chaired by Kebbi State Governor, Nasir Idris. NEC acknowledged the sector’s potential to stimulate economic growth, create employment and improve livelihoods across the country. It noted that all states had indicated interest in supporting the Federal Government’s livestock development initiatives and resolved to strengthen collaboration between federal and state governments to accelerate reforms and unlock the sector’s economic potential. FG, States To Establish Joint Financing Framework For CNG, Electric Vehicles Council also considered a presentation on the National Affordable Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) Transit Programme by the Chairman of the Presidential Initiative on Compressed Natural Gas and Electric Vehicles, Ismaeel Ahmed. It resolved to establish a joint financing framework between the Federal and State Governments to accelerate the deployment of CNG and electric vehicles across the country. NEC directed that the programme must deliver tangible benefits to citizens through reduced transportation costs, rather than limiting its impact to the provision of alternative-energy vehicles. It also resolved that relevant authorities should engage transport unions and operators to ensure that savings from the adoption of CNG and electric vehicles are passed on to commuters through lower fares. item.title: 'Marvel’s Wolverine' Soars on PS5 Sales Charts Despite Negative Buzz
item.description: Don’t believe everything you see on the internet. After Marvel’s Wolverine became a laughingstock on social media, with widely circulated clips blasting the game’s “fart trail” UI and lackluster chase sequences, the game seems to have done quite well from a sales perspective . According to new data from industry analyst group Circana, Marvel’s Wolverine was September's best-selling game in the United States across physical and digital. Not bad for a console exclusive with an already infamous reputation.

item.title: Meta shocked by $25B fine after N.M. refused to join multistate settlement
item.description: Meta must pay $25 billion to New Mexico after a jury found the tech giant guilty of nearly 44 million violations of state consumer protection laws. The largest fine to ever hit Meta came after New Mexico Attorney General Raúl Torrez declined to join an $18 billion settlement Meta reached earlier this year with attorneys general in nearly all states. In his opinion Wednesday, US district court judge Francis J. Mathew said there was no “bright line rule” for determining the appropriate penalty for Meta's repeated and willful deception of users since 2010 about their “control of data, third-party data misuse, misinformation, hate speech, and equal enforcement.” Read full article Comments

item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US at Nu Stadium on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage Concacaf on Thursday announced it has approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg against the United States on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of the capital of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the US, had been booked for Kingston. The Grenadiers played their 2026 World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.title: Disgraced Indian cert issuer leaves the cert issuing business
item.description: After embarrassing reports revealed weak private keys, one of which was just a single digit, Indian certification authority eMudhra has decided to take the L and get out of the global SSL/TLS cert game entirely. eMudhra announced Thursday that it was abandoning that arm of its business. Sure, the intense scrutiny heaped on the company was a factor, but the firm also argued that growing compliance costs and competition from free certificate providers had made the business increasingly difficult to justify. “Global SSL/TLS is a small part of eMudhra’s business contributing to about 1 percent of the global revenue,” the company explained, noting that free SSL/TLS cert issuance from large firms and increased compliance and data sovereignty requirements have made it a minor part of the firm’s operation, and one that doesn’t merit so much bad press. “The level of social media amplification around this incident has brought scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business,” eMudhra explained. “In view of this, after detailed deliberations our board has concluded that withdrawing from global SSL/TLS is the right decision for eMudhra and its shareholders.” An argument could be made that, even if SSL/TLS accounts for just 1 percent of its global revenue, a private CA key with a value of 4 still deserves a thorough public shaming. It’s only been two days since eMudhra’s weak private keys were exposed in public reports , following a report to Mozilla on October 17, and it wasn’t exactly hard for security researchers to recover them: The eight affected private-key values ranged from the number 4 (yes – a plain old number 4), to 56 and 66, to the far more complicated 115, 155, 156, 230, and 237. No quantum computer required to crack those keys. Wow – better save the qubits . item.content:encoded: After embarrassing reports revealed weak private keys, one of which was just a single digit, Indian certification authority eMudhra has decided to take the L and get out of the global SSL/TLS cert game entirely. eMudhra announced Thursday that it was abandoning that arm of its business. Sure, the intense scrutiny heaped on the company was a factor, but the firm also argued that growing compliance costs and competition from free certificate providers had made the business increasingly difficult to justify. “Global SSL/TLS is a small part of eMudhra’s business contributing to about 1 percent of the global revenue,” the company explained, noting that free SSL/TLS cert issuance from large firms and increased compliance and data sovereignty requirements have made it a minor part of the firm’s operation, and one that doesn’t merit so much bad press. “The level of social media amplification around this incident has brought scrutiny that is out of proportion to SSL/TLS’s place in our business,” eMudhra explained. “In view of this, after detailed deliberations our board has concluded that withdrawing from global SSL/TLS is the right decision for eMudhra and its shareholders.” An argument could be made that, even if SSL/TLS accounts for just 1 percent of its global revenue, a private CA key with a value of 4 still deserves a thorough public shaming. It’s only been two days since eMudhra’s weak private keys were exposed in public reports , following a report to Mozilla on October 17, and it wasn’t exactly hard for security researchers to recover them: The eight affected private-key values ranged from the number 4 (yes – a plain old number 4), to 56 and 66, to the far more complicated 115, 155, 156, 230, and 237. No quantum computer required to crack those keys. Wow – better save the qubits . This wasn’t just an embarrassing collection of numbers, either: The weak keys belonged to eight intermediate certificate authorities, potentially allowing attackers to forge certificates trusted by systems that hadn’t blocked them. eMudhra, however, maintains that the affected CAs had issued no end-entity certificates. eMudhra quickly went on the defensive about its mind-boggling key-management failure, acknowledging the weak keys while pointing to independent audits and a problem during its key-generation ceremony that it said produced the weak keys alongside the intended strong ones. “A flaw in the key generation ceremony caused a wrap/unwrap step to produce a second set of weak keys alongside the original strong keys,” the company said the day after the key fiasco was reported. “The weak keys were the ones published to the browser root stores.” Despite that, eMudhra said the relevant certificate infrastructure had undergone two years of independent audits and had been in browser trust lists since mid-2025, raising questions about why the weak keys weren't caught sooner. eMudhra claimed on Thursday that the affected CAs had issued no end-entity certificates, that it had revoked those CAs within 14 hours of discovering the issue, and that neither its infrastructure nor its data had been compromised as a result of its key boo-boo. Still, the incident has given eMudhra another reason to shave off a small part of its business rather than continue facing scrutiny over its certificate operations. It’s still going to issue a root-cause report and fulfill its remaining commitments to browser root programs as it winds down the business. The company said it’ll continue to serve G1 RSA roots until it transitions customers to other certificate issuers, which it will do free of charge. “Revocation and certificate status services will keep running until every issued certificate has expired or been replaced,” the company said. ®

item.title: Video Game Industry Responds to BioWare Shutting Down
item.description: Electronic Arts revealed on Wednesday that the legendary RPG studio BioWare is no more . The sudden shuttering wasn't exactly a surprise to onlookers — recent BioWare releases received mixed reviews and middling sales numbers — but deep down, many were hoping that the developer could find its footing again. Seemingly every gamer and industry worker of a certain era still has fond memories of surviving Mass Effect 2 's suicide mission, or romancing a character in Dragon Age: Origins .

item.title: Websites across world hit by millions of attempts to exploit PHP code flaw
item.description: Problem in language that underpins 70% of sites has led governments and companies to pull sites offline to patch fault Tell us: have you been affected by the PHP code flaw? What is PHP, and how bad is the computer language flaw causing website shutdowns globally ? Websites around the world have been hit by millions of attempts to exploit a recently discovered vulnerability in their code, cybersecurity companies have said, as the US warned the flaw could allow attackers to take control of web servers, steal data and disrupt services. The problem in the PHP programming language, which underpins about 70% of the world’s websites, emerged on Wednesday causing governments and companies to pull their websites off the internet before they could be attacked and so they could patch the fault. Continue reading...

item.title: US-backed vaccine trial on babies canceled after international outcry
item.description: Government officials in Guinea-Bissau have formally rejected a clinical trial that would be run by Danish researchers and funded by the US to look for alleged nonspecific harms from the newborn dose of the hepatitis B vaccine. The vaccine dose is currently recommended globally for all newborns and has been used safely and effectively for decades. In an email to Ars Technica, one of the trial's lead researchers, Christine Stabell Benn of Bandim Health Project and the University of Southern Denmark, said that Guinea-Bissau's Council of Ministers "formally reaffirmed its non-acceptance of the study on 16 October." The revelation that the study was formally rejected last week comes after news on Monday that judicial police in Guinea-Bissau raided Bandim Health's offices and seized vaccines . Stabell Benn highlighted that the police search came after the trial was rejected. Read full article Comments

item.title: Ahead of US and Israeli elections, 3-day joint attack on Iran 'would not radically change conflict'
item.description: Jean-Emile Jammine is pleased to welcome Federico Donelli, Associate Professor of International Relations in the Department of Political and Social Sciences at the University of Trieste in Italy. Can another three days of military strikes achieve what eight months of confrontation have failed to deliver? Donelli challenges the assumption that a short, intensive offensive would necessarily produce a decisive political outcome. He argues, "the real question is whether military pressure is intended to constrain Iran's capacity, or to pressure Iran to sit on the table." And whether they can translate that capacity into a sustainable political outcome without provoking a wider regional crisis. Regardless, Donelli reminds us that "Iran still has leverage over the US."

Huang (University of San Francisco); Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) A sweeping barred spiral galaxy marks the spot in this image, but the real treasure is the gravitational lens in the lower-right corner, where a distant background galaxy is being magnified and distorted by the gravity of a closer galaxy. This observation is one of many gravitational lensing images taken by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope in preparation for science with the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope . Gravitational lensing occurs when the mass of a foreground object – such as a galaxy – warps spacetime, causing light to bend, distort, and magnify as it passes around the object, similar to a giant lens in space. Lenses like this occur when a precise chance alignment takes place between the foreground and background galaxies, causing light from the background galaxy to curve around the foreground galaxy. In this image, the gravitational lens features a foreground elliptical galaxy that is about 4.5 billion light-years away. That means the light we see from this galaxy now would have first started traveling toward us when our solar system was still forming. The background galaxy is about eight billion light-years away, almost twice as far. It appears as a pair of arcs, one large and very noticeable to the upper left of the foreground galaxy, the other a much smaller, flipped image of the same background galaxy to the lower right. This configuration is called an arc-counterarc pair. The background galaxy magnified and made visible by this gravitational lens appears twice in this image ― as a large arc and smaller, flipped arc ― on opposite sides of the elliptical foreground galaxy. item.content:encoded: Explore Hubble Hubble Home Overview About Hubble The History of Hubble Hubble Timeline Why Have a Telescope in Space? Hubble by the Numbers At the Museum FAQs Impact & Benefits Hubble’s Impact & Benefits Science Impacts Cultural Impact Technology Benefits Impact on Human Spaceflight Astro Community Impacts Science Hubble Science Science Themes Science Highlights Science Behind Discoveries Universe Uncovered Hubble’s Partners in Science Hubble & Citizen Science SI & Hubble Science Explore the Night Sky Observatory Hubble Observatory Hubble Design Mission Operations Science Operations Astronaut Missions to Hubble Hubble vs. Webb Hubble vs. Roman Team Hubble Team Career Aspirations Hubble Astronauts Multimedia Images Videos Online Activities e-Books Sonifications Podcasts 3D Hubble Models Lithographs Fact Sheets Posters Hubble on the NASA App Glossary News Hubble News Social Media Media Resources 35th Anniversary More Online Activities 4 min read NASA’s Hubble Charts Path for Roman with Gravitational Lenses A sinuous spiral galaxy (center) appears in the same field of view as a vivid gravitational lens (right corner) in this Hubble image. The lens consists of a reddish elliptical foreground galaxy and the blue arcs of a magnified background galaxy. NASA, ESA, and X. Huang (University of San Francisco); Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) A sweeping barred spiral galaxy marks the spot in this image, but the real treasure is the gravitational lens in the lower-right corner, where a distant background galaxy is being magnified and distorted by the gravity of a closer galaxy. This observation is one of many gravitational lensing images taken by NASA’s Hubble Space Telescope in preparation for science with the new Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope . Gravitational lensing occurs when the mass of a foreground object – such as a galaxy – warps spacetime, causing light to bend, distort, and magnify as it passes around the object, similar to a giant lens in space. Lenses like this occur when a precise chance alignment takes place between the foreground and background galaxies, causing light from the background galaxy to curve around the foreground galaxy. In this image, the gravitational lens features a foreground elliptical galaxy that is about 4.5 billion light-years away. That means the light we see from this galaxy now would have first started traveling toward us when our solar system was still forming. The background galaxy is about eight billion light-years away, almost twice as far. It appears as a pair of arcs, one large and very noticeable to the upper left of the foreground galaxy, the other a much smaller, flipped image of the same background galaxy to the lower right. This configuration is called an arc-counterarc pair. The background galaxy magnified and made visible by this gravitational lens appears twice in this image ― as a large arc and smaller, flipped arc ― on opposite sides of the elliptical foreground galaxy. NASA, ESA, and X. Huang (University of San Francisco); Processing: Gladys Kober (NASA/Catholic University of America) The more massive the foreground galaxy is, the stronger the gravitational lens and the more significantly it bends light. By studying the distortion of the background galaxy, researchers can determine how much mass the foreground galaxy contains. This plays a huge role in the study of dark matter, the mysterious, invisible substance that makes up the majority of mass in the universe. The visible matter is not enough to account for the level of distortion in the background galaxy, which allows researchers to calculate both the mass of the foreground galaxy and how much dark matter it contains. Almost all of the objects in this image are galaxies, except for a few scattered foreground stars. The barred spiral galaxy in this image – so called because its arms extend from a bar of stars in its center – is about the size of our own Milky Way galaxy, which astronomers think is a barred spiral as well. The tiny spiral to the left of the large spiral may be a satellite galaxy, similar to the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds that orbit the Milky Way. Hubble views the cosmos primarily in visible and ultraviolet light with some infrared coverage, and Roman sees mainly infrared wavelengths and some visible light. Hubble can provide high-resolution views of individual objects, while Roman has a much larger field of view conducive to panoramas. Images like this offer a glimpse of how Hubble and Roman will work together to build an even more comprehensive picture of the cosmos. This is just one of many gravitational lens images captured by Hubble. Astronomers will use them to analyze gravitational distortions to learn more about dark matter in the foreground galaxies and to lay the groundwork for future Roman observations. Hubble can only view these gravitational lenses one at a time, while Roman’s wide view of the sky will provide a greater sample of these lenses. Astronomers are using Hubble’s sharp images to build a computer model to better analyze dark matter-induced distortions. This tool will help astronomers analyze Roman’s large images. Hubble will also follow up on interesting lenses Roman detects. Hubble vs. Webb Hubble and Webb observations complement each other, providing us with a broad view of the universe. What Did Hubble See on Your Birthday? item.title: 2027: ‘Political Opponents Aren’t Enemies,’ John Momoh Cautions Against Divisive Rhetoric
item.description: As campaigns for the 2027 general elections in Nigeria gather momentum, the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Channels Media Group, Dr. John Momoh, has urged political parties to refrain from utterances capable of fuelling disunity in the country. Momoh, who stated this while presenting a keynote address titled, Narratives That Build Nations In Diversity, Public Relations Leadership And The Future of Nigeria, at the 38th Dr. Sam Epelle Gold Paper Lecture in Yola, Adamawa State, on Thursday, noted that a “divisive appeal to ethnicity or religion can turn a neighbour into a suspect”. ﻿ He explained that democracy needs vigorous debate, disagreement, scrutiny and the freedom to challenge those who govern, adding that political opponents should not be seen as enemies of the nation. “Our politics is charged. The 2027 general elections are approaching, and the competition for power is already shaping public conversation. Political parties are building alliances, candidates are making claims, supporters are mobilising, and citizens are deciding whom they believe,” Momoh said at the event where Governor Ahmadu Fintiri was also unveiled as Patron of the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR). “Democracy needs vigorous debate. It needs disagreement, scrutiny and the freedom to challenge those who govern. But disagreement should not become permission to dehumanise. Political opponents are not enemies of the nation. “Critics are not automatically traitors. Supporters are not exempt from the duty to tell the truth. In a tense season, words can become fuel. “A false allegation can travel through a community before the person accused has a chance to respond. A divisive appeal to ethnicity or religion can turn a neighbour into a suspect. And a manipulated video or an invented quotation can harden opinions before the facts are known,” he added. Leadership Matters Stressing the importance of leadership, the CEO explained that political leaders and public figures have the reach to calm a moment or inflame it. “They can reject language that invites violence, correct claims made by their own supporters, and remind people that the contest for office must not destroy the country we all share,” he added. On the economy, Momoh said that the credibility of any economic story “depends on whether citizens can find evidence of progress in their own lives”. According to him, the economy also has its own powerful narrative because people feel it at the kitchen table. “Families weigh the cost of food, transport, rent, school fees, power and healthcare. item.dc:creator: Alexander Okere
item.content:encoded: As campaigns for the 2027 general elections in Nigeria gather momentum, the Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Channels Media Group, Dr. John Momoh, has urged political parties to refrain from utterances capable of fuelling disunity in the country. Momoh, who stated this while presenting a keynote address titled, Narratives That Build Nations In Diversity, Public Relations Leadership And The Future of Nigeria, at the 38th Dr. Sam Epelle Gold Paper Lecture in Yola, Adamawa State, on Thursday, noted that a “divisive appeal to ethnicity or religion can turn a neighbour into a suspect”. ﻿ He explained that democracy needs vigorous debate, disagreement, scrutiny and the freedom to challenge those who govern, adding that political opponents should not be seen as enemies of the nation. “Our politics is charged. The 2027 general elections are approaching, and the competition for power is already shaping public conversation. Political parties are building alliances, candidates are making claims, supporters are mobilising, and citizens are deciding whom they believe,” Momoh said at the event where Governor Ahmadu Fintiri was also unveiled as Patron of the Nigerian Institute of Public Relations (NIPR). “Democracy needs vigorous debate. It needs disagreement, scrutiny and the freedom to challenge those who govern. But disagreement should not become permission to dehumanise. Political opponents are not enemies of the nation. “Critics are not automatically traitors. Supporters are not exempt from the duty to tell the truth. In a tense season, words can become fuel. “A false allegation can travel through a community before the person accused has a chance to respond. A divisive appeal to ethnicity or religion can turn a neighbour into a suspect. And a manipulated video or an invented quotation can harden opinions before the facts are known,” he added. Leadership Matters Stressing the importance of leadership, the CEO explained that political leaders and public figures have the reach to calm a moment or inflame it. “They can reject language that invites violence, correct claims made by their own supporters, and remind people that the contest for office must not destroy the country we all share,” he added. On the economy, Momoh said that the credibility of any economic story “depends on whether citizens can find evidence of progress in their own lives”. According to him, the economy also has its own powerful narrative because people feel it at the kitchen table. “Families weigh the cost of food, transport, rent, school fees, power and healthcare. A promising economic indicator matters, but citizens want to know whether their lives are becoming more manageable,” he said. “The World Bank reported that Nigeria’s real GDP grew by 4.2 per cent in the first half of 2026. The Central Bank’s figures showed year-on-year headline inflation easing to 14.63 per cent in September from 15.39 per cent in August. “These are positive movements. But when inflation falls, prices may still be rising, only at a slower pace. It does not mean that the cost of living has returned to what families could afford before.” Speaking further, the media chief stated, “This distinction matters for public communication. If an official says that inflation has eased, and a family hears that food is still more expensive, the family is not being unreasonable. The two statements can both be true. Good leadership explains the difference and keeps working on the effect people actually feel. “Growth must mean more than a number. It must become decent jobs, dependable public services, wages that can support a household, opportunity for young people, and confidence that the effort to build a life is worthwhile. The credibility of any economic story depends on whether citizens can find evidence of progress in their own lives.” Promoting Security Momoh also emphasised the need for intelligence, training, coordination, and public support to strengthen security agencies in the country. “Security is an even more immediate measure. Across the country, communities face insurgent violence, banditry, kidnapping, communal conflict, farmer–pastoralist tensions and other threats. In Adamawa and the wider North-East, insecurity has disrupted homes, farming, education, livelihoods and family life,” he said. “We must speak of these realities with care. Behind every statistic is a person: a child who cannot attend school, a farmer afraid to return to a field, a family forced from its home, a community unable to reach a clinic. Their experience must not be reduced to a talking point in a political argument. “Our security agencies need intelligence, equipment, training, coordination and public support.” The chief executive further stated that communities need protection and a reason to trust that reports will be heard. Justice must follow crime, and prevention must accompany response. “A government’s account of security will be judged by whether people can live, work, travel, learn and sleep without fear,” said Momoh. “These are not easy stories to tell. But a good national narrative does not hide difficult truths. It gives them names, identifies responsibility, reports what is being done, and allows citizens to see whether the response is working.” On governance, he urged political leaders to match words with action for the benefit of the citizens “Every government tells a story about its purpose. It may speak of renewal, reform, development, security or opportunity. But the public does not assess that story by the words alone. People compare it with their lived experience,” he stated. “When leaders promise a road, citizens watch to see whether it is built. When government promises relief, people ask whether it reaches those who need it. When officials announce a reform, families want to understand why it is necessary, what it will cost them, what support is available, and what success will look like. “Good communication therefore begins with the quality of the decision. If a policy has not been thought through, if its impact has not been understood, or if those who carry its cost have not been heard, communication cannot repair the weakness. It may postpone the reckoning, but it will not remove it.” “Leadership must make room for honest advice before decisions are announced. It must ask: who will benefit? Who may be harmed? What evidence supports this choice? What will we do if the expected result does not come? How will we explain the trade-offs without talking down to the public? “The public also needs to see that leaders accept responsibility. If a project is delayed, say why and give a credible timeline. If a service fails, acknowledge it and explain how the failure will be addressed. If a claim was wrong, by all means correct it. A leader’s willingness to repair a mistake can strengthen trust more than pretending the mistake never happened,” he added. Mohom commended Governor Fintiri for the achievements recorded in Adamawa. “I would like to acknowledge the work your administration is doing to transform Adamawa. Investment in roads and urban renewal, public buildings, schools and healthcare facilities is changing the state’s landscape and strengthening access to public services,” he said. “These efforts deserve recognition, and the people of Adamawa deserve a clear account of what has been completed, what is under way and what remains to be done.” He described Epelle as one who understood that communication goes beyond sending out information and encompasses the work of building understanding and confidence between an institution and the people it serves. The post 2027: ‘Political Opponents Aren’t Enemies,’ John Momoh Cautions Against Divisive Rhetoric appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: 'Cabin leak suspected': Artemis II astronaut reveals how a warning nearly derailed NASA's epic moon mission
item.description: null TENERIFE, CANARY ISLANDS — NASA's Artemis II astronauts were just minutes away from a critical engine burn that would send them toward the moon when an unexpected cabin leak warning threatened to change the course of their historic mission. "If it had happened five minutes later, we may not have been able to have that burn," Artemis II pilot Victor Glover revealed during an Oct. 18 discussion with Canadian former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival here in Tenerife. The incident unfolded on April 2, the second day of the Artemis II mission, as the astronauts' Orion spacecraft swooped back toward Earth after traveling some 38,000 miles (61,000 kilometers) away. Orion had been completing a highly elliptical orbit around Earth , giving the crew and mission control an opportunity to test the capsule's systems before committing to the journey to the moon . Orion was now approaching its closest point to our planet, roughly 100 miles (160 km) above the surface, ahead of the crucial translunar injection (TLI) burn that would send the astronauts moonward. "Jeremy looks out the window and says, 'I think we're going to run smack dab into the middle of Earth,'" Glover recalled, referring to Artemis II mission specialist Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency . "Because we were getting so low." The close approach brought additional challenges, as Orion passed through a region populated by orbital debris and satellites. "The density of things is going up from where we are, and also an increase in radiation," Glover explained. It was at this particularly demanding point in the mission that Orion issued a warning that indicated a possible cabin leak, around 15 minutes before the critical TLI burn. "So, determining whether it was real or not was a big deal," Glover said. The crew and mission control faced a crucial question: Was it safe to continue heading to the moon , or would they have to abandon the planned maneuver and cut the mission very short? "Are we going to do a TLI and burn to go to the moon, or are we putting on our spacesuits to prepare to come back to Earth right now?" Glover recalled. The timing was particularly critical. The TLI burn was designed to propel Orion out of Earth orbit and onto its trajectory around the moon, marking the first time astronauts had headed toward Earth's nearest neighbor since the Apollo era. The moon, seen here backlit by the sun during a solar eclipse on April 6, 2026, captured by one of the cameras on the Orion spacecraft's solar array wings. (Image credit: NASA) Luckily, as NASA flight director Judd Frieling told us during an April 2 media briefing , the warning turned out to be a false alarm. So Artemis II received the go-ahead. Orion fired its main engine for approximately five minutes and 50 seconds, successfully setting the four astronauts on their journey around the moon. "We're watching the timer count down, velocities go up, and the magenta and green numbers coming together," Glover

item.content:encoded: null TENERIFE, CANARY ISLANDS — NASA's Artemis II astronauts were just minutes away from a critical engine burn that would send them toward the moon when an unexpected cabin leak warning threatened to change the course of their historic mission. "If it had happened five minutes later, we may not have been able to have that burn," Artemis II pilot Victor Glover revealed during an Oct. 18 discussion with Canadian former astronaut Chris Hadfield at the Starmus VIII festival here in Tenerife. The incident unfolded on April 2, the second day of the Artemis II mission, as the astronauts' Orion spacecraft swooped back toward Earth after traveling some 38,000 miles (61,000 kilometers) away. Orion had been completing a highly elliptical orbit around Earth , giving the crew and mission control an opportunity to test the capsule's systems before committing to the journey to the moon . Orion was now approaching its closest point to our planet, roughly 100 miles (160 km) above the surface, ahead of the crucial translunar injection (TLI) burn that would send the astronauts moonward. "Jeremy looks out the window and says, 'I think we're going to run smack dab into the middle of Earth,'" Glover recalled, referring to Artemis II mission specialist Jeremy Hansen of the Canadian Space Agency . "Because we were getting so low." The close approach brought additional challenges, as Orion passed through a region populated by orbital debris and satellites. "The density of things is going up from where we are, and also an increase in radiation," Glover explained. It was at this particularly demanding point in the mission that Orion issued a warning that indicated a possible cabin leak, around 15 minutes before the critical TLI burn. "So, determining whether it was real or not was a big deal," Glover said. The crew and mission control faced a crucial question: Was it safe to continue heading to the moon , or would they have to abandon the planned maneuver and cut the mission very short? "Are we going to do a TLI and burn to go to the moon, or are we putting on our spacesuits to prepare to come back to Earth right now?" Glover recalled. The timing was particularly critical. The TLI burn was designed to propel Orion out of Earth orbit and onto its trajectory around the moon, marking the first time astronauts had headed toward Earth's nearest neighbor since the Apollo era. The moon, seen here backlit by the sun during a solar eclipse on April 6, 2026, captured by one of the cameras on the Orion spacecraft's solar array wings. (Image credit: NASA) Luckily, as NASA flight director Judd Frieling told us during an April 2 media briefing , the warning turned out to be a false alarm. So Artemis II received the go-ahead. Orion fired its main engine for approximately five minutes and 50 seconds, successfully setting the four astronauts on their journey around the moon. "We're watching the timer count down, velocities go up, and the magenta and green numbers coming together," Glover recalled. "Everything is tracking. It's looking good." Before long, the crew had broken free of Earth's gravitational hold and were hurtling toward the moon at around 24,500 mph (39,430 kph). Despite the tense moments before the burn, Artemis II went on to make history. NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman (the mission's commander), Glover (pilot) and Christina Koch (mission specialist), along with Hansen, traveled farther from Earth than any humans before them, reaching a maximum distance of 252,756 miles (406,771 km) during their journey around the moon. The four astronauts returned safely to Earth on April 10, splashing down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego after nearly 10 days in space.

item.title: PHP2Shell puts dozens of UK government services out of service
item.description: The PHP2Shell security fiasco has forced 32 UK government services offline and left another four partially unavailable as Whitehall scrambles to patch the critical vulnerabilities wreaking havoc across the web. The figures were disclosed in the House of Lords on Thursday, where tech minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra outlined the disruption following the discovery of two critical flaws in PHP . "Currently, the information I have is that 32 government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable," Lloyd told peers. "That has resulted largely from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied." "We are working very carefully with departments to restore the services safely and securely following that remediation activity," she added. Whitehall has not published a full list of affected services, although the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) is among those known to have taken their websites offline, rather inconveniently with next week's Budget looming. Peers also raised reports of disruption affecting the DVLA and police services. Britain isn't alone in pulling the plug. Government websites in Germany, France, Belgium, Finland, and the Netherlands have also been taken offline as a precaution, along with Australia's own cybersecurity agency website. Across the Atlantic, the NSA has urged organizations to patch or disconnect vulnerable systems, although the US government has not publicly confirmed any website shutdowns. PHP2Shell comprises two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on vulnerable servers. The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) warned organizations to patch immediately or consider pulling affected systems offline until they could be fixed. "The NCSC was briefed by OpenAI last week on this potential specific vulnerability and has been working to ensure that disclosure happened in a co-ordinated way with vendors, so there was sufficient preparation to protect customers," Lloyd said. Security firm Calif found one of the PHP bugs using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model, while Google's Wiz separately uncovered both flaws with the help of AI tools. OpenAI then dug into the vulnerabilities itself and worked with vendors and government agencies to get the word out. The government established a cross-departmental incident response operation before public disclosure, Lloyd said. The NCSC also sent 50,000 warnings to businesses and other organizations. The disruption has spread beyond central government. Liberal Democrat peer Baroness Ludford pointed to several councils whose services had reportedly been taken offline, including Edinburgh, Oxford, Bristol, Lambeth, and Barnet. She questioned why central government and local authorities remain outside the statutory duties proposed under the government's Cyber Security and Resilience Bill , which returns to the Lords on Monday. item.content:encoded: The PHP2Shell security fiasco has forced 32 UK government services offline and left another four partially unavailable as Whitehall scrambles to patch the critical vulnerabilities wreaking havoc across the web. The figures were disclosed in the House of Lords on Thursday, where tech minister Baroness Lloyd of Effra outlined the disruption following the discovery of two critical flaws in PHP . "Currently, the information I have is that 32 government services are unavailable and four are partially unavailable," Lloyd told peers. "That has resulted largely from precautionary measures taken to protect systems while security updates and mitigations are applied." "We are working very carefully with departments to restore the services safely and securely following that remediation activity," she added. Whitehall has not published a full list of affected services, although the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) is among those known to have taken their websites offline, rather inconveniently with next week's Budget looming. Peers also raised reports of disruption affecting the DVLA and police services. Britain isn't alone in pulling the plug. Government websites in Germany, France, Belgium, Finland, and the Netherlands have also been taken offline as a precaution, along with Australia's own cybersecurity agency website. Across the Atlantic, the NSA has urged organizations to patch or disconnect vulnerable systems, although the US government has not publicly confirmed any website shutdowns. PHP2Shell comprises two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, that could allow unauthenticated attackers to execute code on vulnerable servers. The National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC) warned organizations to patch immediately or consider pulling affected systems offline until they could be fixed. "The NCSC was briefed by OpenAI last week on this potential specific vulnerability and has been working to ensure that disclosure happened in a co-ordinated way with vendors, so there was sufficient preparation to protect customers," Lloyd said. Security firm Calif found one of the PHP bugs using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol model, while Google's Wiz separately uncovered both flaws with the help of AI tools. OpenAI then dug into the vulnerabilities itself and worked with vendors and government agencies to get the word out. The government established a cross-departmental incident response operation before public disclosure, Lloyd said. The NCSC also sent 50,000 warnings to businesses and other organizations. The disruption has spread beyond central government. Liberal Democrat peer Baroness Ludford pointed to several councils whose services had reportedly been taken offline, including Edinburgh, Oxford, Bristol, Lambeth, and Barnet. She questioned why central government and local authorities remain outside the statutory duties proposed under the government's Cyber Security and Resilience Bill , which returns to the Lords on Monday. "We are not currently aware of any confirmed compromise of central government systems resulting from these vulnerabilities," Lloyd told peers, later extending that assessment to the wider UK public sector. AWS says attackers were exploiting the flaws four days before they were publicly disclosed , while Cloudflare has since recorded millions of attempts to weaponize them. ®

item.title: This emulator reimagines Nintendo’s Virtual Boy with a full color display
item.description: Last year, we reported on Red Viper , a Virtual Boy emulator that added a splash of Super Game Boy-style color to Nintendo's famously failed red-on-black "portable" 3D headset from the '90s. Now, a new emulation experiment, VBoy Color , has taken the concept to a higher level, using a tile-based palette system that allows for many more distinct colors in each individual Virtual Boy frame. Rather than simply replacing the Virtual Boy's four shades of red with four different colors, VBoy Color's readme files explain how the emulator's game-specific Color Packs can assign a distinct four-color palette to each 8x8 tile in a Virtual Boy scene. That means the emulator can differentiate between green pipes, grey platforms, and red brick wall in Mario Clash , for instance, even though all those in-game objects share the same overlapping red hues in the original game. The Game Boy Color-esque results feel like being transported into an alternate history where Nintendo invested in a full-color display rather than cheaper red LEDs for the Virtual Boy hardware. The increased contrast between differently colored elements is particularly welcome in games like Jack Bros. or Vertical Force , where the original red-on-red display often makes it hard to differentiate the player-character from busy red background elements. Read full article Comments

item.title: Ukraine and Russia exchange strikes after US envoy visit to the Kremlin
item.description: Ukraine and Russia exchanged drone and missile strikes on Thursday, killing seven people in Ukraine, according to authorities. Moscow said it had intercepted 630 Ukrainian drones targeting the Russian capital. The strikes came hours after US envoy Steve Witkoff met Vladimir Putin in St. Petersburg. Witkoff said Moscow was ready to resume trilateral talks with Kyiv and Washington.

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...
